#1760. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1757. Chelsea in the race? Nico Paz sets the 2027 transfer market alight, but who can actually afford him?

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 07:02, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 07:03

Among the best-performing players in Europe since the start of the season, Nico Paz is the dream of many of the continent’s heavyweights. But a three-figure sum in millions (more than £85m / €100m) will undoubtedly be needed to sign the Argentina international.

Nico Paz was the star of the show as Como thrashed RC Lens 9-1 in the Champions League on Wednesday. A key figure for the Italian side for three seasons, the Argentine number 10 lit up the game with his talent, scoring one goal and providing two assists. In his last five outings, the 22-year-old has even accumulated five goals and five assists.

Unsurprisingly, the best clubs on the planet are battling to secure his services and one of them has a competitive advantage: Real Madrid. Real Madrid hold a buy-back clause of £68m (€80m), included when he was sold to Como in 2024 for £56.1m (€66m). It cannot, however, be activated before next summer.

Real Madrid are therefore the favourites to bring back their former player at such a price, while other European giants will probably find it harder to compete.

It is easy to imagine that Como will not sell their star cheaply and will ask for at least £85m (€100m) to let Nico Paz go to another club. That sum seems too high for Barcelona, who have not spent such an amount since 2019, when they signed Antoine Griezmann.

Because of the sanctions that still threaten the club, Manchester City also appear to be out of the running for now. Their rivals Manchester United, meanwhile, have clearly lost some of their lustre and would probably be less attractive in the eyes of the Argentine.

A transfer to Paris Saint-Germain cannot be ruled out, given that the double reigning European champions have the means to pull out such a big sum. Furthermore, the playing philosophy put in place by Luis Enrique would probably appeal to the Argentina star.

The Premier League also remains an avenue to consider. While Liverpool have Florian Wirtz in this role, Chelsea, for their part, are not afraid of stacking up talents (and expensive transfers) and, despite the presence of Cole Palmer, it would not be so surprising to see Chelsea join the race.

For now, Real Madrid appear to be in pole position to sign him in the summer of 2027, but this saga could heat up in the coming months if Nico Paz continues to perform this well.

#1756. Man City are not a team in Enzo Maresca's ideal image yet - their imperfections are clear as win at Leipzig shows they're learning on the job, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 5 November 2026

Watching Manchester City is not exactly straightforward at the moment. Downright confusing most of the time. Different tweaks on the same tactical theme each week, City learning on the job under new management.

Enzo Maresca recently revealed that he would rather win games 1-0 than these helter-skelter, drama-filled, error-strewn goal fests but they are not yet capable of producing that. And the players know it.

On leading in Saxony, secured by Castello Lukeba's own goal, Maresca called for Phil Foden and Abdukodir Khusanov to sprint for the bench to receive detailed instructions. As they did, Marc Guehi and Enzo Fernandez engaged in deep conversation. Gesturing arms as Erling Haaland and Elliot Anderson spoke while walking back to halfway.

The body language was as if they had gone behind. Strangely, that might encourage the boss. They know this all can improve drastically in a quest to become more cohesive. There is definitely the talent among the squad to possess a certainty of how to emphatically dominate games like this one.

None of this is particularly different to when they went on the seven-game winning run to fly out of the blocks in the Premier League, imperfections making them eminently watchable but not a team in Maresca's ideal image yet. Not by a long shot.

Later, when Anderson and Rayan Cherki were locked in debate about how to press from a goal kick, it served as a reminder of Maresca's words that this is a fresh project and change takes time. Chinks exist.

Erling Haaland came to Manchester City's rescue once more with the winning goal at Leipzig

He slid home City's winner with minutes remaining after fine work from Elliot Anderson (left)

Yet on the surface this presentable a creditable result, won by Haaland with 12 minutes left as they nestle inside the Champions League's top eight. All good for now, although added confusion comes in how little this could all mean amid an appeal of the independent commission's findings. Nobody is dissecting Maresca's evolving masterplan if they lose in court.

'We need to step up,' said Haaland, captain for the night. 'Keeping the ball, knowing when to keep it and when to go, working together offensively and defensively.'

Maresca himself admitted to shaking up the midfield and back four because he is feeling out a best XI, one he can rely upon and one that mixes that quintessentially City dominance and a more direct attacking line that can punish in a nanosecond.

'I need to understand more things about the players,' he said. 'That's why I'm so confident because I'm sure that we're going to be better and better.'

Coached by one of the Italian's closest friends and former City centre-half Martin Demichelis, Leipzig felt they deserved more. They went behind in unfortunate circumstances, although Enzo Fernandez lurked at the back post to do the honours from Nico O'Reilly's drilled cross had Lukeba not completed the job for him.

And Gianluigi Donnarumma was offering encouragement, almost embarrassed by Antonio Nusa's shot squirting through his fingers. Among other opportunities, Christoph Baumgartner curled wide from the box's edge. Baumgartner had oceans to himself amid a vacant City midfield. Anderson had gone to put out a fire out wide, vacating his holding position.

Anderson was operating there alone on the night, not something he has done regularly since a £116million summer switch, and it presented yet another iteration of Maresca's City as he attempts to locate the perfect formula.

Then two minutes summing up Donnarumma. Full stretch to acrobatically tip another Baumgartner shot wide seconds after the restart. And yet, shortly after, suffering one of those moments that are becoming far too common.

In an entertaining game, City took the lead initially when Castello Lukeba scored an own goal

Ridle Baku (right) equalised for Leipzig just after half-time due to a Gianluigi Donnarumma error

Enzo Fernandez restored City's lead with this emphatic header after Iliman Ndiaye's cross

Antonio Nusa saw Leipzig equalise for a second time before Haaland decided the game late on

RB Leipzig (4-2-3-1): Vandevoordt 6; Baku 7 (Henrichs 74, 6), Orban 6, Lukeba 4, Raum 6; El Aynaoui 6 (Seiwald 74, 6), Baumgartner 7 (Nkunku 57, 6), Banzuzi 6; Gruda 7, Romulo 6 (Gomis 67, 6), Nusa 7 (Reitz 73, 6)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Nunes 6 (Dias 79), Khusanov 6, Guehi 6, O'Reilly 6; Anderson 8 (Bouaddi 83); Foden 6 (Doku 64, 6), Fernandez 6 (Kovacic 83), Cherki 7, Ndiaye 7 (Allan 83); Haaland 7

Ridle Baku was the beneficiary of the goalkeeper's poor positioning, forgetting about his near post, and flashed in. Somebody of Donnarumma's standing cannot allow that to happen. He would soon fumble another Baku shot, which led to a penalty appeal.

'It is not a concern but it is a mistake,' Maresca said. 'Before that he did a save that no other keeper in the world makes. Gigio knows he was not good with the goal. He's going to do better.'

City missed plenty of chances themselves before Fernandez headed in a second from Iliman Ndiaye's whipped cross but that lead only lasted three minutes, Nusa slamming into the far corner just after the hour. 'Silly goals,' Maresca said.

City kept ploughing forward, Anderson kept driving on. Ndiaye set Anderson storming down the right and he knew the area to hit. Back post, Haaland. A wicked cross, a striker's finish. Game won. Maybe that's what they were chatting about earlier.

#1755. Fabrizio Romano reveals Liverpool's stance on Giorgi Mamardashvili

Giorgi Mamardashvili's Liverpool transfer was met with mixed reviews.

The goalkeeper was initially signed during the 2024-25 season for around £30 million.

However, he spent the entirety of that campaign on loan to Valencia as, at the time, the Reds still had Caoimhin Kelleher among their ranks.

In the end, the Georgian replaced Kelleher and, unfortunately, things haven't been that smooth sailing.

He played 20 games for Liverpool last term and, although his performances were fairly spotty, he was still a decent option.

Rumours about his future started to emerge after Alisson's contract was extended this summer and now, the Reds' stance on the Georgian's future has been revealed.

Fabrizio Romano confirms Liverpool are happy with Giorgi Mamardashvili

Even though fans could tell that Mamardashvili was nowhere near as good as Kelleher last term, he's still managed to stick around.

However, that could end up changing in the near future as the Reds have recently decided to spend £30 million on KRC Genk 'keeper, Lucca Brughmans.

The Belgian is only 18 years old but, he's already a regular starter for Genk and has been putting in some top-notch displays this term.

Thanks to this, fans are now wondering what plans Liverpool's hierarchy have in store for their squad this season with Fabrizio Romano now sharing an insight into what the Reds' fanbase have to look forward to in the future.

"There is a serious possibility this could be Alisson’s last season at Liverpool. Nothing is decided, but there is interest from several countries and he could explore those opportunities," he shared via his YouTube channel.

"Liverpool knew he was considering Juventus last summer. They extended his contract for a further season and he decided to stay.

"It’s still very early, and Liverpool could ask him to stay at the end of the season. The club are also really happy with Mamardashvili."

Liverpool must figure out if Giorgi Mamardashvili is their next Alisson

Alisson has been Liverpool's starting goalkeeper for as long as anyone can remember.

The Brazilian has been a rock between the sticks at Anfield and, when he hasn't been played, the weaknesses among Liverpool's ranks has been exposed.

In fact, there have actually been several games where Alisson's performances have single-handedly earned the Reds their points.

A lot of their success has come from how strong Alisson has been and, having Virgil van Dijk in front of him has obviously also helped with that.

Right now, most fans can't see how Mamardashvili could plug the gap left by Alisson but, if Liverpool can, they need to figure out a way to prove that to fans.

Otherwise, some serious questions are going to need to be asked.

Or, a lot of money will need to be spent trying to replace the Brazilian which, in reality, isn't all that feasible at the moment, especially since they just splashed £30 million on Brughmans in summer.

#1754. 'Lacklustre' - Raphinha slammed by Spanish media despite Barcelona comeback win vs Atletico Madrid

By Lewis Blain | 09 Nov 2026 07:03

Barcelona came from behind to secure a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano on Sunday evening, with Fermin Lopez scoring twice to preserve their position at the top of LaLiga.

However, Raphinha endured a frustrating night against Diego Simeone's side, struggling to make an attacking impact as Atletico's defenders successfully restricted his influence.

The Brazilian received predominantly negative reviews from the Spanish media, with two publications awarding him 5/10 and another giving him 6/10, although his pressing and work rate were acknowledged.

El Nacional were particularly critical, awarding Raphinha 5/10 and describing him as "desaparecido" - 'disappeared'.

Gerard Romanach felt the Brazilian barely featured, writing: "Raphinha hoy no ha aparecido. Muy bien defendido por los centrales, tampoco ha tenido ninguna ocasion clara para marcar." In English, 'Raphinha did not turn up', with Atletico's centre-backs defending him well and preventing him from finding a clear goalscoring opportunity.

ElDesmarque also handed him 5/10, although they recognised his contribution without the ball, highlighting his pressing as particularly important to Barcelona's second-half improvement.

La Vanguardia were slightly more generous, awarding Raphinha 6/10 and labelling him "controlado" - 'contained'. They felt Atletico successfully defended the winger, restricting his involvement and preventing him from becoming a significant attacking threat.

Mundo Deportivo described him as "desajustado" - 'out of sync' - suggesting he fell into Atletico's trap by drifting into crowded central areas rather than finding space out wide. Nevertheless, the publication stressed that his effort and commitment were unquestionable.

Meanwhile, Barcelona-focused publication Comuniate also described his display as "bastante gris" - rather 'lacklustre' - and English-based Barca Universal gave him 6.5/10, noting that he struggled to influence proceedings against Atletico's defensive organisation.

Despite the criticism, there is little reason for Barcelona to become overly concerned about Raphinha's form based on one frustrating evening.

The Brazilian has enjoyed an outstanding start to the 2026-27 campaign, registering 19 goals and three assists in 14 appearances across LaLiga and the Champions League. His return includes 15 league goals and four in Europe's premier club competition, underlining just how influential he has been for Hansi Flick's side.

That exceptional productivity makes Sunday's performance look more like an isolated setback than a worrying decline. Atletico deserve credit for successfully restricting him, but Raphinha still contributed through his pressing and defensive work, even when his attacking qualities were largely neutralised.

Barcelona also found other solutions, with Fermin stepping up to score twice and Lamine Yamal providing the decisive assist. That ability to win without Raphinha firing on all cylinders is another positive for Flick.

The 29-year-old has set exceptionally high standards this season, but his 22 goal contributions provide plenty of evidence of his importance. One quiet night against Simeone's notoriously difficult defensive setup should not overshadow what has otherwise been an electric campaign.

#1753. Amorim opts against press conference ahead of Genoa vs. Milan – the reason

There will be no pre-game press conference with Ruben Amorim today, as confirmed by Milan’s press office yesterday.

It was hard to miss Amorim’s disappointment and anger after Milan’s defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday evening, being very honest in his interview after the game. While he took on some of the blame, he criticised the players for not having the right attitude and mentality.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s something that has been echoed by others, including the Milan legend Billy Costacurta, who criticised the entire squad for not doing the red and black shirt justice. In any case, the Rossoneri need to get back on the horse on Sunday, taking on Genoa away from home.

As confirmed by Milan’s press office last night, in a message sent directly to us and other news outlets, there won’t be any press conference with Amorim today. It’s something he usually hosts on the eve of each game, but there is a reasonable explanation for the cancellation.

Generally speaking, we are not huge fans of Amorim opting to cancel the press conference, but it comes down to the congested schedule. He spoke to the media before and after the Ferencvaros game, so he didn’t feel like a press conference less than 48 hours later would give much.

It’s not the first time a press conference has been cancelled this season due to that very reason, and it’s something we have seen with other managers at Milan too. In other words, it was kind of expected even if, without a doubt, the journalists would have had questions for Amorim.

#1752. Report: Liverpool to beat Barcelona to £75m Virgil van Dijk replacement

Virgil van Dijk is undoubtedly one of the best defenders in history, but his time at Anfield cannot last forever.

The legendary Liverpool captain is into the final 12 months of his deal, and as things stand will be leaving Merseyside for free in the summer.

At 35-years-old, the Dutchman has played every minute of the Reds' Premier League campaign so far, in what could be his final season at Anfield.

Julian Ward and Liverpool's recruitment team have already begun planning for a potential departure, and one star is now reportedly being lined up for a massive £75 million move.

Barcelona to battle Liverpool for Premier League defenderSeveral of Europe's top defenders have been identified as potential replacements for Liverpool's skipper, but one move now gaining traction is for Chelsea's Levi Colwill. The 23-year-old has started all but one of the Blues' Premier League games this season, captaining his side on three occasions. Now, the Reds are lining up a move that could cost as much as £75 million to bring the five-capped England international to Merseyside.

Several of Europe's top defenders have been identified as potential replacements for Liverpool's skipper, but one move now gaining traction is for Chelsea's Levi Colwill.

The 23-year-old has started all but one of the Blues' Premier League games this season, captaining his side on three occasions.

Now, the Reds are lining up a move that could cost as much as £75 million to bring the five-capped England international to Merseyside.

That's according to a report from Caught Offside, which claims that Liverpool hold a strong interest in the defender and will try and convince him to consider a new challenge.

The report states that Chelsea want to keep Colwill at Stamford Bridge but that they could consider a bid of between £65-75 million.

Liverpool aren't the only team interested in the 23-year-old however, with La Liga leaders Barcelona also monitoring the situation.

Chelsea would likely be more willing to deal with a team in another league rather than selling one of their best players to a direct rival, but if the Reds can make an attractive enough offer then they may be able to land their man.

Colwill has been on the radar at Anfield for some time, and Liverpool could finally act on their long-term interest to replace Van Dijk, should the Dutchman leave in the summer.

#1751. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1749. Nottingham Forest: ‘Only way you can beat Man City’ – Glasner reveals formula for shock win

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 07:16

Oliver Glasner did not hide his pride at Nottingham Forest’s performance in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday at the City Ground, in the 10th round of the Premier League.

After claiming their first home win of the season, the manager highlighted defensive intensity, tactical intelligence and the ability to take advantage of the right moments to attack as decisive factors against a side he considers one of the toughest to face in English football.

‘I think it is the only way you can beat Man City. They’re so good, such great players, such a good structure and they move the ball so quickly. They can play through the middle, they have incredible dribblers on the wing and they have such pace. Then, of course, they have Haaland in the middle,’ Glasner explained.

The Austrian manager stressed that it is not enough to wait for the opponent to retreat or to limit oneself to protecting one’s own area. To compete against a squad with so many attacking alternatives, Forest had to maintain concentration throughout the match and show intensity in their marking, without giving up on attacking when space opened up.

‘You should control everything and if you want to control it, you have to run because you have to be so quickly aware. Of course you can just defend but you also need to go forward and this is what we did today in the right moments, we scored the goals in the right moments and credit again to the players,’ he said.

The strategy paid off at the City Ground. Jair Cunha opened the scoring, and Liam Delap doubled the advantage before Manchester City pulled one back. The striker later scored again, securing the 3-1 win that Forest needed as much for the impact on the table as for the confidence of the squad.

Glasner, however, was keen to remind everyone that a result of this size cannot be treated as predictable against Manchester City. The manager attributed the win to the commitment of the players and the atmosphere created by the supporters over the 90 minutes.

‘You can never plan to win 3-1 against City because they are so good. But today, especially the players and our fans deserve this win because they were so passionate from the first minute, scoring nice goals.’

The support from the stands was also important in the moments when Forest had to resist the pressure from the visitors. For Glasner, the team found strength precisely in the combination of collective work on the pitch and the encouragement received at the City Ground.

‘We had moments to suffer but then we could rely on our fans pushing us, supporting us. Amazing goals and such a great team effort today so really proud.’

Despite his satisfaction with the result, Glasner did not necessarily consider the win to be Nottingham Forest’s best performance with the ball.

The manager acknowledged that his side had little possession and that, in other matches, they have shown more elaborate football. The difference, this time, was the willingness to defend and the ability to execute the plan against a high-level opponent.

‘I think we’ve had better performances in possession because today we rarely had the ball. Regarding the team spirit, the energy, I think it was our best game.’

The Austrian once again highlighted the way Forest behaved without the ball, especially the discipline required to contain Manchester City’s movements. In the manager’s assessment, the combination of passion, organisation and tactical reading allowed the hosts to withstand the moments of pressure and turn their chances into goals.

‘The way we play football I think we’ve had many better games but how we defended, how passionately we defended, how tactically smart we defended, it was one of our better games,’ he concluded.

The win took Forest to nine points in the Premier League and took the team out of the relegation zone, at least provisionally. As well as ending the wait for a first home win of the season, the result represents an important boost for a squad trying to regain ground in the competition. For Glasner, the display against Manchester City showed a possible path: intensity, organisation and efficiency in the decisive moments.

#1748. Opinion: Liverpool handed major transfer boost in chase for £45m sensation

Liverpool were probably expecting their squad to be completed by now.

They've spent over £600 million on new players across the last couple of seasons and, if we're being honest, things still aren't great.

Multiple areas of of Andoni Iraola's squad have failed to meet the standards expected of them and have forced fans to question whether some of the players that their team have signed were even worth buying in the first place.

This thought process has led to different questions being asked about their first-team squad and has caused many players to be linked with a move.

And now, the Anfield outfit seem to have just been handed a major boost in their pursuit for one of their main targets.

Barcelona want to sign Levi Colwill which could open the door for a Ronald Araujo transfer

Ronald Araujo has arguably been one of Liverpool's best signings this season.

The Uruguayan was brought in on a season-long loan with the Reds having an option to buy worth €55 million (£45.9 million).

This may not seem like all that much money with how good the centre-back has been but, since he'll be 28 years old by the time Liverpool can activate their option to buy, it's unclear whether he'll be worth them signing or not.

Obviously, things such as his injury history also need to be taken into consideration.

But, luckily for Liverpool, a fresh update from Caught Offside has shared that Barcelona now want to sign Levi Colwill from Chelsea.

"Barcelona view Colwill as a top target after studying his performances and stats in great detail, there have been internal discussions about putting a bid together, possibly as early as this January," they wrote.

Levi Colwill could be Barcelona's replacement for Ronald Araujo

With how happy Araujo seems to be at Liverpool and how happy the Reds' fanbase seems to be with the Uruguayan, a permanent deal for him makes sense.

His ability to play as a right-back or a centre-back is massive with both of those areas major problems for Liverpool at the moment.

In fact, their whole defence could do with a re-jig.

Barca are likely to stick to their price of €55 million for Araujo but, if they manage to get a deal over the line for Colwill before then, they could become a little more lenient.

Araujo's experience is unmatched compared to some of the other players that Liverpool have been linked with.

But, only time will tell whether the Reds feel like a move for the 27-year-old is worth it.

#1747. Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EST, 5 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended  meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

#1746. Tottenham transfer news: Spurs now set to rival Man Utd for £33m left-back target in January window

By Lewis Blain | 09 Nov 2026 07:26

Tottenham Hotspur are considering a move for Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde ahead of the January transfer window.

The 22-year-old is expected to explore an exit from Camp Nou, with super-agent Jorge Mendes sounding out several Premier League clubs.

Manchester United are among those interested, but Spurs could now enter the race for a defender who may be available on loan.

Balde's future at Barcelona is increasingly uncertain as the player's representatives are speaking to several sides, with the Premier League viewed as the Spaniard's preferred destination, per reports in Spain.

Liverpool, Aston Villa and United have all listened to the terms of a potential deal, while Spurs and Manchester City are also being considered.

Barcelona would ideally like to secure a permanent exit worth around €40m (£33m), but Mendes reportedly believes a loan with an option-to-buy could be a more realistic solution.

That option could become mandatory if certain conditions are met, allowing Barcelona to free up salary space immediately while potentially securing a significant future fee.

The LaLiga giants are keen to use any departure to create room in their wage budget ahead of January recruitment. A decision is expected in December, with Mendes assessing the available projects before determining the best option for his client.

Both Tottenham and United have reasons to consider a move for the Barcelona defender.

United have been desperate for greater reliability at left-back, with Luke Shaw's recurring injury problems making it difficult to depend on him throughout a full campaign.

Meanwhile, in north London, Destiny Udogie has yet to provide the consistency the club would have hoped for, while relying on an ageing Andy Robertson would hardly represent a long-term solution.

Balde, meanwhile, offers a younger option with experience at the highest level and the potential to develop into a first-choice defender.

An initial loan arrangement could also make the deal more appealing to both Premier League clubs, particularly if Barcelona are willing to include an option-to-buy.

United may have a more obvious need, but Spurs could also benefit considerably from adding a player with Balde's attacking qualities and experience.

With Mendes exploring the English market, this is a transfer situation worth monitoring closely as January approaches.

#1743. Opinion: Andoni Iraola's very own Ibrahima Konate has been found

Andoni Iraola's time as Liverpool manager has been a bit of a roller coaster so far.

The Spaniard took over at the start of July and, although the Reds did fairly well in their pre-season games, that same level of performance hasn't really followed them through to the actual season.

So far, the Reds have lost three games across all competitions and have failed to fill their fans with any sort of confidence that things can be turned around.

And, with the transfer window now just around the corner, fans have started to question what sort of moves Liverpool could make to improve their fortunes.

Indeed, Liverpool may have already spent around £600 million on new players over the last couple of seasons but, with the level of player they're being linked with, it feels like a lot more than that is going to be spent.

Liverpool have re-ignited their interest in Castello Lukeba

Ibrahima Konate's departure during the 2026-27 summer transfer window was one that many fans expected.

For the last couple of years, talks between the Frenchman and Liverpool about a new contract had taken place but, each time either party was asked about negotiations, nobody could give a definitive answer about whether an agreement was going to be reached.

This led fans to realise that Konate's time was up, especially when it was announced that Jeremy Jacquet would be joining Liverpool for £55 million.

From that point on, fans have come to grips with the loss of the Frenchman and have tried to source a new player to plug the gap.

That's where RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba comes in.

As per a fresh update from FootballFanCast, Liverpool are now the most likely team to sign Lukeba.

"Football FanCast sources understand that Liverpool are currently the most interested Premier League club in signing RB Leipzig centre-back Castello Lukeba," they wrote.

"The 23-year-old has attracted attention from several leading English sides, with Arsenal having monitored his development for an extended period and Manchester United also expressing interest.

"However, Liverpool are understood to have emerged as the strongest suitors, and sources understand the Frenchman's representatives have informed all three suitors of his desire to move to the Premier League."

Castello Lukeba could become Andoni Iraola's version of Ibrahima Konate

Looking back at Konate's time with Liverpool, there were definitely some highs and lows.

The Frenchman won the Premier League twice and the Champions League once but, towards the end of his time at Anfield, he was making some rather silly mistakes.

Whether he was misplacing passes or mistiming challenges, some fans were happy to see him go.

But, when he was at his best, Konate was easily one of the Premier League's best centre-backs.

This is exactly who Lukeba could become. Not only is he another French centre-back from RB Leipzig but he's also a similar age to when Konate left Leipzig for L4 back in 2021.

Much like Konate, Lukeba also has a release clause within his Leizpig contract and, although his is worth a bit more than Konate's was, it feels like 23-year-old has a lot of potential to fulfil.

Of course, these are just rumours at the moment but, of all the centre-backs linked with Liverpool ahead of the January transfer window, Lukeba is one of the deals that makes the most sense.

By Lewis Blain | 09 Nov 2026 07:48

Crystal Palace are preparing for life without Pierre Sage, with the Frenchman facing mounting pressure following another damaging defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Eagles sit bottom of the table after losing four consecutive league matches, leaving the club two points adrift of safety.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford boss Thomas Frank has emerged as the leading candidate to take over at Selhurst Park.

Sage's position is increasingly precarious after a 3-1 defeat at Selhurst Park left Palace rooted to the foot of the Premier League.

The Eagles have now suffered four successive league defeats by an aggregate score of 12-1, while their defensive record has become a major concern after conceding 24 goals in their opening 10 matches.

There had already been concerns within the club about Sage's appointment before the campaign began, despite his impressive work in France with Lens and Lyon.

Palace are set to sack manager Pierre Sage following their 3-1 defeat by Liverpool. Result leaves them bottom of the Premier League after a complete round of games for the first time since December 2017 #CPFC @TheAthleticFC https://t.co/kIVduqHpYC

The 46-year-old guided RC Lens to second place in Ligue 1 last season and won the Coupe de France, but he has struggled to translate that success into results in England.

Sage, appointed on a three-year contract in June, insisted after the Liverpool loss that his own position was not his priority, instead stressing the need to find an effective solution for the club.

He has reportedly been promised significant investment in the squad during January should he accept the position, potentially giving him the opportunity to address Palace's shortcomings.

Frank is arguably a more proven option in English football than Sage, but the quality and balance of the squad remain major concerns - even an experienced appointment will need substantial backing if Palace are to climb away from the relegation zone.

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

Online casino company BC Game, who has been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season, announced its partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this week.

The promotional video, which was laced with innuendo and featured Elfie receiving a package from a delivery man containing her partnership contract, was accompanied with the caption: 'Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin.'

The Foxes Trust has reacted angrily to the shirt sponsor’s association with Elfie, who has also built a following in Esports and competitive online gaming communities.

In a furious statement titled 'BC Game - It gets worse', the fan body said: 'Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the Trust's dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.

'BC Game have now announced a new partnership with "international content creator and Esports personality" Eva Elfie... who just happens to be an international porn star.

Leicester City supporters have expressed fury and dismay after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its new ambassador

Casino firm BC Game has been Leicester's primary shirt sponsor since the 2024-25 season

Welcome to BC Game @EvaElfie! Let the fun begin 😏 pic.twitter.com/xzLJ4uBOx7

'From the moment the Club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values. 'The Club has not only partnered with a gambling company, but chosen one that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, has unanswered questions about the legitimacy of its funding and its origins, and allows clients to "game" using cryptocurrencies.

'Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

Focusing on Elfie's esports portfolio in his announcement, BC Game chief executive Ali 'Ako' Muhanned said: 'Eva has built an incredible relationship with the gaming and esports community through genuine passion and consistent content creation.

'At BC.GAME, we want to work with creators who understand how to entertain, connect with audiences in real time, and bring positive energy to our players. Her live streams are dynamic and engaging, making her a natural fit as we expand our footprint across esports and interactive entertainment.'

Elfie, who has 4.8million followers on Instagram, also released her debut single 'Fairyland' last month.

Since partnering with BC Game, the Foxes have plummeted down the football league, suffering back-to-back relegations from the Premier League to League One.
