#1688. Liverpool receive new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update as Hungary issue social media statement

By Ben Knapton | 09 Nov 2026 11:05

Liverpool have received a new Dominik Szoboszlai injury update from the Hungarian FA, who have announced that the midfielder is undergoing further tests on Monday.

Szoboszlai completed 69 minutes of Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace in Sunday's Premier League fixture, setting up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal before being withdrawn for Trey Nyoni.

Reds head coach Andoni Iraola revealed after the game that Szoboszlai was not feeling 100%, though, as the Hungary international appeared to be struggling with a knee problem at Selhurst Park.

Szoboszlai has nevertheless joined up with his national team for the time being, as the Magyars prepare to face Georgia and Northern Ireland in a pair of Nations League fixtures this month.

However, the Hungarian FA revealed on X on Monday morning that the Liverpool lynchpin is being examined by medical staff, although it remains to be seen whether he will pull out of the ranks.

"@_SZD10, who was substituted in the 69th minute of Liverpool FC’s match yesterday, is undergoing tests today, Monday, following the usual protocol in such cases," the Hungarian FA wrote. "We will, of course, keep the public informed of developments as soon as possible!"

Hungary sit second in League B Group 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, a standing which would see them qualify for the promotion playoffs taking place next March.

The Magyars are just one point below leaders Northern Ireland, though, and clinching top spot would see Hungary promoted to League A for the next cycle.

Szoboszlai started each of Hungary's four Nations League games in the September/October international break, captaining his country to successive victories over Georgia and Ukraine in their most recent two fixtures.

However, the 26-year-old then returned to Liverpool with a hamstring problem, ruling him out of the 3-0 home defeat to Manchester City, although he was fit enough to make his comeback against Brentford the following week.

Szoboszlai exacerbated his injury at the Gtech Community Stadium, though, and subsequently missed fixtures with LASK Linz, Villarreal, Chelsea and Brighton & Hove Albion, but Liverpool won all four games in his absence.

Szoboszlai made it through the entirety of the 2025-26 season without suffering a single injury - playing 53 games in total - and he only missed two matches in 2024-25 due to illness.

The 26-year-old did suffer a pair of hamstring injuries in 2023-24, ruling him out of 10 Liverpool matches in total, while his most serious injury occurred during his time with RB Leipzig.

Szoboszlai joined the German giants while recovering from a serious adductor problem, meaning he did not make his debut until eight months after joining in August 2021, having arrived in December 2020.

The midfielder has since amassed 31 goals and 27 assists in 158 matches for Liverpool, whose first game back after the hiatus comes at home to bitter rivals Manchester United on November 22.

#1685. Long balls are NOT banned at Newcastle! Matthias Jaissle insists his criticism after Everton defeat was lost in translation - having said stars were failing to follow tactics

Published: 11:50 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 5 November 2026

Matthias Jaissle says his criticism of Newcastle’s players was lost in translation and has clarified that long balls are not forbidden under his management.

The head coach also believes that his squad understands what is being asked of them, although he says his door remains open to any player seeking clarity over his instructions.

In the wake of Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Everton, Jaissle said that the players had failed to follow his instruction and bemoaned their use of long balls when the plan was to keep it on the floor.

Asked if those comments had been addressed with the squad this week, Jaissle said: ‘I don't know if it's a misinterpretation or a language barrier, but there is an element of that when I explained that in the press conference.

‘But it is indeed (something) we address, because we talked sometimes about the no-risk zone, where we had previously critical-ball losses leading to goals. Of course, if there is a clear risk for ball loss, then I prefer playing a long ball to our striker and protecting the ball and develop the game from there.

‘It (my comments) are not to point any fingers, not at all. Sometimes you are willing to do something, but on that day it just did not work and you make the wrong decisions. It comes also with confidence.

Matthias Jaissle, pictured giving instructions during Newcastle's defeat by Everton, has insisted long balls are not banned

'If you have scenarios where you can find easily your team-mate on the ground and we build up from there with our patterns, then you should for sure also prefer that.

‘But it's not easy, it's easier said from outside. If the confidence is missing, then you prefer to be really safe and shooting maybe even more the long ball.’

Daily Mail Sport was told this week that some players are ‘confused’ by exactly what it is Jaissle wants from them, but the head coach said: ‘The fundamental thing is that we can count on unity and togetherness.

'The door is always open if ever there is anything unclear. If you see the training then I’m pretty sure everyone understands and is fully committed. There was never a question, at least I’m not aware of it.

‘It’s important we listen to the players. If there is anything unclear, they will drop in.’

Meanwhile, Jaissle says he retains the support of the club’s hierarchy after a run of four defeats in five matches.

‘The nice part is that I got even more the feeling from within the club how committed they are (this week),’ he said.

‘That just shows me that everyone believes in the long-term project and that everyone is also aware and realistic about the journey and where we are right now.’

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 11:17, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 11:20

Oxford United welcome Cheltenham Town to the Kassam Stadium on Tuesday night for their second EFL Trophy group match of the campaign, while the visitors will be playing their third and final fixture in the group.

Both sides head into the contest on the back of FA Cup first-round fixtures, with the U's suffering a 1-0 defeat to Stevenage on Saturday afternoon, while the Robins booked their place in the next round with a 2-0 home victory over Halifax Town.

After spending two seasons in the Championship, Oxford United were relegated last May and entered the 2026-27 campaign among the favourites for promotion as they looked to secure an immediate return to the second tier.

Aaron Ramsey's side have made a positive impression back in League One so far, winning seven, drawing five and losing just once in their opening 13 matches to climb into third place.

Oxford also have a game in hand on the top two and could move level on points with league leaders Huddersfield Town by winning their rearranged fixture, although the Terriers' superior goal difference would likely keep them at the summit.

Given their impressive league form, it is perhaps surprising that Ramsey's side head into Tuesday's encounter having lost all three of their cup matches this season, following an EFL Cup defeat to Leyton Orient, a penalty shootout loss to Exeter City in this competition and, most recently, their FA Cup exit at the hands of Stevenage on Saturday.

However, the Welshman, who made 86 appearances for his country, fielded a much-changed side against the Boro at the weekend, underlining that securing promotion back to the Championship remains his main priority.

As for Cheltenham Town, they have entered the 2026-27 campaign as a League Two side for the third consecutive season and are aiming to mount a serious promotion challenge after dropping out of the third tier in 2024.

Former Bristol City manager Steve Cotterill arrived last season and guided the Robins to an 18th-placed finish, but his first full campaign in charge has started on a much more positive note.

Although Cheltenham have lost three of their last six matches, they currently sit fifth in the table after collecting 21 points from 14 games, even if their recent results have allowed leaders Salford to establish a substantial advantage at the summit.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, the Robins have enjoyed success in the cup competitions so far, winning both of their EFL Trophy group matches on penalties before progressing to the next round of the FA Cup on Saturday.

Goals from Jake Evans and George Miller helped Cotterill's side secure a 2-0 victory over National League outfit Halifax Town, ensuring they avoided a potential cup upset.

Having made wholesale changes at the weekend and rested several first-team regulars, Ramsey is likely to rotate his squad again and could name a side similar to the one that started Saturday's FA Cup defeat.

Simon Eastwood has featured in both matches since Jamie Cumming was sent off during a league fixture and could retain his place in goal on Tuesday night.

Captain Cameron Brannagan is expected to be rested once again, with Tyler Goodrham and Harrison Bradney among the most likely candidates to feature in midfield.

Cheltenham are also expected to make wholesale changes, particularly after Cotterill told Robins supporters "to stay home".

Joe Day was forced off after just 19 minutes of their most recent EFL Trophy fixture but has since returned to the substitutes' bench and could be restored to the starting lineup for this contest.

Former Aston Villa forward Andreas Weimann is expected to sit this one out, leaving George Miller to lead the line.

Eastwood; Long, Lacey, Golding, Leigh; Missanga, Bradney, Goodrham, Snowden; Lynch, O'Donkor

Cheltenham Town possible starting lineup:

Day; Tomkinson, Wilson, Sweeney, Nurse; Stevenson; Bickerstaff, McWilliams, McCann, Otchere; Miller

With both sides enjoying positive campaigns near the top of their respective divisions, we expect a closely fought encounter, despite the gap between them in the football league pyramid.

However, Oxford should have enough quality to claim their first cup victory of the season, and we are backing the League One side to edge a narrow 2-1 win.

#1679. Nations League permutations: What do England need to qualify for quarter-finals?

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 11:37, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 11:39

Eight teams will secure their spot in the quarter-finals of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League, with the group stage of the competition set to conclude this month.

Two sides have already booked their spot in the final eight - Spain and Portugal - and they will soon be joined by six more, with the quarter-finals set to take place in March 2026.

England are currently second in Group A3 behind Spain, with the Three Lions on the brink of securing their position in the final eight of the tournament.

The top two in each of the four groups will qualify for the quarter-finals.

Here, Sports Mole runs through the various permutations for the four groups.

France currently sit at the top of Group A1, with the Blues picking up 10 points from their four matches courtesy of a record of three wins and one draw.

Italy, meanwhile, are second on seven points, with their record in this group standing at two wins, one draw and one defeat.

Belgium are third in the section on six points courtesy of a record of two wins and two defeats, while Turkey are bottom, losing all four of their games thus far.

France host Italy on November 12, and a victory would see them qualify automatically ahead of their final game against Turkey. However, a draw with Italy would leave them on 11 points, with a win then required against Turkey to make sure of qualification.

A loss to Italy would mean that France need to beat Turkey to make sure of a spot in the final eight; two defeats, though, could see Zinedine Zidane's side finish third.

Italy would qualify if they manage to beat both France and Belgium, while beating France and then drawing with Belgium would also put them in a strong position.

A draw with France and then overcoming Belgium could also potentially be enough, but if Italy lose to France, they would need to beat Belgium and hope for favourable results elsewhere.

Italy cannot afford to lose both matches if they are to finish in the top two.

Belgium, meanwhile, would qualify if they beat both Turkey and Italy; a win over Turkey and a draw with Italy could also be enough depending on results elsewhere.

Should Belgium draw with Turkey, they would still be alive but would need other results to go their way, but a loss in either match makes it incredibly difficult for them to finish in the top two.

Turkey, meanwhile, are bottom of the section and cannot reach the top two.

Group A2 is incredibly close, with Netherlands at the top of the section on eight points, level with second-placed Greece heading into the final two matches.

Germany, meanwhile, are third in the section on five points, with Serbia fourth on zero points.

A win for Netherlands against Greece on November 13 would see them reach 11 points and leave them in a very strong position to secure a spot in the quarter-finals.

A draw with Greece then a positive result against Germany could also secure qualification for the quarter-finals, but a defeat to Greece would leave them needing a positive result against Germany and also results elsewhere to go in their favour.

Wins for Netherlands against both Greece and Germany would make sure of a position in the final eight, so that will be the goal for Xavi's side.

Greece, meanwhile, would be on 11 points with a win over Netherlands, which would leave them in a very strong position in the group ahead of the final round of matches.

A draw with Netherlands would leave them on nine points ahead of their final game with Serbia, where a win would book a spot in the final eight.

However, a loss to Netherlands would leave Greece needing to beat Serbia and then hope that Germany cannot overtake them; wins over both Netherlands and Serbia would see Greece secure a position in the quarter-finals of the tournament.

As for Germany, the national team must beat Serbia to keep their qualification hopes alive, but they would also then need to secure a positive result against Netherlands.

Anything less than four points from their final two matches makes qualification incredibly unlikely, but wins in both would take them onto 11 points, which could be enough to make the top two.

Serbia, though, are bottom of the section on zero points and cannot qualify.

Spain are top of Group A3, winning each of their four matches to collect 12 points, while England are second in the section, gathering nine points from their four games.

Croatia are third on three points, while Czech Republic are at the bottom on zero points.

Spain are already through to the quarter-finals of the tournament, and a win over Czech Republic on November 12 would secure first spot in the section.

England, meanwhile, are almost certainly in the quarter-finals; Croatia need to beat them 8-0 on November 12 to stand a chance of jumping above them in the section on the head-to-head record.

Mathematically, at this stage, England need a point to qualify, but sitting six points ahead of third-placed Croatia, it is incredibly difficult to imagine them not being present in the final eight.

Croatia lost 7-0 to England on October 3 and need to win 8-0 in their next match to have a realistic chance of progressing, with a victory over Czech Republic also required, in addition to a favour from Spain against England in the final fixture.

Czech Republic, though, are bottom of the section on six points and cannot qualify.

Portugal are already through to the knockout round of the tournament, picking up 12 points from their four matches, while Denmark are second, claiming six points from four matches.

Wales sit third in Group A4 on three points, while Norway are fourth on three points, so it is all to play for in the final two matchdays of the tournament.

Portugal can, in theory, still finish second in the section behind Denmark, but avoiding defeat against the Danes would secure first spot in the group.

Denmark need four points from their final two matches in the group against Portugal and Norway to be sure of a spot in the quarter-finals, but three points may also be enough depending on potential head-to-head tie-breakers.

Wales' route into the final eight is difficult given that they have lost both games against Denmark, who therefore have the advantage in any head-to-head tiebreaker.

The Dragons must beat both Norway and Portugal to stand a chance of finishing in the top two, but they are also relying on results elsewhere.

Norway also need to beat both Wales and Denmark, which would give them nine points, while a victory over Denmark would be important, as they would lead the head-to-head tie-breaker.

Two wins from their final two games would put them in a position to qualify, and they have a clearer route than Wales through that avenue despite currently sitting fourth.

#1678. Liverpool Confidential: Billionaires' investment set to beat deadline, new deal for Trey Nyoni, the academy kids who shone in Istanbul and Mor Talla Ndiaye's visa issues

Published: 12:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:04 EST, 5 November 2026

The deal for a group of billionaires to buy a minority stake in Liverpool remains on track to pass a deadline set by the new independent football regulator.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia, known as 1892 Holdings, agreed to purchase a 38 per cent stake in Fenway Sports Group’s controlling interest in the club earlier this season. And despite some anxieties externally and in the fanbase about a lack of updates, I have been told this week that everything is moving in the right direction.

Sources close to Bhatia and his consortium insist the process takes time but there are no hitches and it is still expected to beat the deadline. It is understood the date in question is in December and in accordance with the new regulator, who must take within 90 days to issue a final suitability determination for prospective new owners or senior executives.

Indeed, this week brought the news that FSG are in exploratory talks to buy a significant stake in Formula One team Cadillac. Both FSG and Cadillac were contacted for comment around that story – and insisted it is an ongoing process.

One source pointed to the fact that FSG clearly expect to have some ‘spare pennies lying around’ – hinting the Liverpool investment will go through.

Senior FSG staff have constantly stressed that selling 38 per cent of the club does not mean they are losing interest and that they are as committed as ever, though the potential for the buy-in to become a full-scale takeover at some point in the future remains.

Bhatia is backed by his billionaire father-in-law Lakshmi Mittal, plus Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin.

Amit Bhatia (second left) is heading up a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool from John Henry (second right) and his Fenway Sports Group

Liverpool supporters hope the deal will transform the club's fortunes on the pitch

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool – and Andoni Iraola ruled him out for more than a month with a problem he suffered at Brentford on October 17.

I understand the Dutch international is now all-but fit and could play this weekend if needed – however, given his high number of injuries, a decision has been made to delay his return.

Liverpool were recently punished for bringing back Dominik Szoboszlai too quickly as the Hungarian pulled up shortly after his first start upon his return, which set him back a fortnight.

Frimpong missed only seven Bayer Leverkusen games through injury in four years at the club according to Transfermarkt, but has already sat out nearly 30 Liverpool matches. Most of those absences have been hamstring related, so Frimpong is not being rushed back and will be given the international break to continue working on his recovery.

Jeremie Frimpong has had rotten luck with injuries since he joined Liverpool and went down again against Brentford last month. However, the Dutch international is now close to a return

Trey Nyoni has been offered a bumper new contract to reward him for his fine progress.

The 19-year-old, who scored his first Liverpool goal in the defeat in Istanbul against Fenerbahce on Wednesday night, has had a stellar rise since Iraola took over at Liverpool.

Nyoni, signed from Leicester City in 2023, was in many matchday squads and featured sparingly last season but has come of age this campaign and has already doubled his first-team minutes – with three quarters of the season still to play.

Nottingham Forest made a £30million bid in the summer but Iraola identified him as a key asset and he will be rewarded handsomely for his progress.

Trey Nyoni scored his first Liverpool goal on Wednesday night in the Champions League loss against Fenerbahce

Your question answered: What's the January priority?

One topic fans have asked me about this week is which position is a priority in the January and summer transfer windows.

The first area to mention is midfield. I have reported in the past how Chelsea are currently ahead of Liverpool in the race for Bournemouth's Alex Scott, so let’s keep an eye on that – and the situation of Lamine Camara of Monaco. But I think the priority has to be a left-back.

Are Milos Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas good enough? Neither have performed at the required level so far this season and bringing Tsimikas back from a loan at Roma – where he barely played – felt like a bit of a cop-out. It has to be a priority position in the next 12 months.

Liverpool flew straight home from Istanbul after the loss to Fenerbahce and did not land on Merseyside until past 2am. It is a departure from last season, when Arne Slot would often have his squad stay for two nights on European away days.

Players are said to be big fans of the extra night at home with most preferring to sleep in their own beds.

Iraola did not hold a post-match team talk after Fenerbahce but will debrief the squad when back in training, having branded the defeat ‘cheap’ and ‘messy’.

Another UEFA Youth League game, another hat-trick for Will Wright.

I was in place on the outskirts of Istanbul on Wednesday afternoon to watch the 18-year-old bag his second treble in four European matches this term, making it 13 goals for the season in all competitions.

Wright had a heated exchange with Josh Sonni-Lambie over who would take a penalty but the pair have smoothed things over now after Wright took it and scored. The striker’s assist for Finn Inglethorpe was also a notable moment that showed he is a team player and not a greedy No9.

Liverpool's Will Wright scored another hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League on Wednesday, against Fenerbahce Under 19s

I was also impressed by right back Oliver O’Connor, who looks like a real athlete. He aced every physical pre-season test for the academy and is versatile, with a quality delivery into the penalty area.

The Scouser joined the club aged six and has been a midfielder for most of his career. Boss Rob Page does not necessarily see him as a right back long-term but he caught the eye up and down that flank.

Those who did watch the academy game – and the first-team later on – would have been wondering where defender Mor Talla Ndiaye was. He is a mainstay in the Youth League XI and has been on the seniors’ bench several times.

It is believed the Senegalese defender had a visa issue and could not feature in the game in Turkey, though next month’s away match in Bruges is not expected to pose the same problem.

Liverpool's Mor Talla Ndiaye (centre) was nowhere to be seen in Istanbul due to visa issues

Also in academy news, young midfielder Michael Laffey has signed with the OmniSports agency who represent the likes of Wright and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton. Under 21s captain Laffey, whose dad owns the Glenbuck pub in Anfield, made the first-team bench a fortnight ago.

Liverpool supporters have drawn the short straw and will pay more than any of their English counterparts for a pint while following their team in Europe this season.

That’s according to data from LiveScore, who have worked out that Reds will pay an average of £4.91 per pint on their travels.

Still, £4.91 for a pint? Better than most places at home. You might need one after watching Liverpool’s defending this week!

#1677. “Being talked about…”: Everton plotting January move for “interesting” England international

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

The comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”

For Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be important. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

The comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January plans. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

#1676. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

Chelsea could make another major investment in their attacking options as they assess potential additions ahead of the January transfer window.

With the Blues continuing to build a squad capable of competing for major honours, Barcelona midfielder Fermín López has reportedly emerged as a player of interest.

The 23-year-old Spain international has attracted attention from several European clubs, with Paris Saint-Germain also considering a move.

Chelsea previously attempted to sign López in 2025, and fresh reports suggest the London club could revisit their interest if the opportunity arises.

According to CaughtOffside, Chelsea and PSG are both prepared to make significant offers for López, who remains an important part of Barcelona’s plans under Hansi Flick.

A source with links to the agents industry told CaughtOffside: “PSG are preparing a serious offer worth around €80million for Fermin Lopez,” before adding: “Chelsea are also considering a massive bid.”

The reported interest could set up a transfer battle between the Premier League side and the French champions. However, neither club has confirmed a formal bid, and any deal would depend on Barcelona’s position and the player’s willingness to leave his boyhood club.

Chelsea are familiar with López, having reportedly made a significant offer for him in the summer of 2025. The midfielder opted to remain at Barcelona, but the latest reports suggest the Blues could be willing to return if his circumstances change.

López’s ability to operate as an attacking midfielder, contribute goals and create chances makes him an appealing option. His performances have also strengthened his reputation as a versatile attacking talent capable of influencing games from advanced positions.

Competition for places at Barcelona could be one factor to monitor, although there is no confirmation that López is actively seeking an exit. CaughtOffside reports that Chelsea and PSG currently have the most concrete interest, while Arsenal and Manchester United have also made enquiries about his situation.

Barcelona, meanwhile, would reportedly prefer to retain the midfielder but could face pressure to consider substantial offers amid their financial challenges. López signed a contract extension in February 2026, keeping him at the club until 2031, meaning negotiations would likely require a significant financial commitment.

Chelsea may also have other priorities for January. The report identifies Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott as a potential focus for the Blues, meaning any pursuit of López could depend on how their wider transfer plans develop.

#1673. Vietnam vs Chinese Taipei - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 09 Nov 2026 11:41

Vietnam play host to Chinese Taipei in an international friendly on Wednesday.

The home side are looking to respond to having failed to defend the FIFA ASEAN Cup, a competition which they have won on the previous two occasions.

While Vietnam are punching above their weight at 99th in the FIFA World Rankings, Kim Sang-Sik's side recently experienced major disappointment.

The four-time winners of the ASEAN Cup, and two-time defending champions, lost 1-0 to Malaysia in the bronze-medal match.

Suffering a 2-1 defeat to Thailand two games earlier had cost Vietnam a place in the final, and it has left Kim with much to ponder.

Prior to that double frustration, Vietnam had been on a remarkable 33-game unbeaten streak, which started in September 2024.

Either side of the Thailand and Malaysia defeats, they had posted a 4-2 triumph over Pakistan.

In sharp contrast, Chinese Taipei - ranked 176th in the FIFA World Rankings - are currently on an eight-match losing streak, which has lasted since 2024.

Wednesday's game is the first time that they have played since March, when they suffered a 3-1 defeat to Sri Lanka.

Across five matches played since September 2025, Chinese Taipei have conceded 20 goals. They have faced Indonesia, Thailand and Turkmenistan during that period.

This is the first encounter between these nations since a 1-1 draw was played out in a friendly in March 2017.

Although Vietnam won the previous games in 2015 and 2016 respectively, Chinese Taipei have scored in all three contests.

Aside from goalkeeper Patrik Le Giang, the other 10 players from Vietnam's last XI do not feature in this squad.

Therefore, Kim's starting lineup is a complete unknown, with our team selection based on players who have already earned caps.

Nguyen Thanh Chung, with 44 appearances, appears likely to start in defence, while Nguyen Dinh Bac has 10 goals from 26 games for his country. There are 11 uncapped players in the squad.

Meanwhile, each of the 11 players that started Chinese Taipei's most recent match in March have been selected in Matt Ross's squad.

Captain Chen Po-liang will earn his 99th cap if he starts this contest. Ivory Coast-born Ange Kouame, with six goals from 17 games for Chinese Taipei, is in line to start as the number 10.

Le Giang; T Nguyen, Phan, N Nguyen, Pham; Khuat, Vo, Le; D Nguyen, T Nguyen, V Nguyen

C Huang; Kuo, Hsu, Baudelet, Tiao; Wu, Chen; Yu, Kouame, Estevez; W Huang

Although Vietnam have lost two of their last three games, we cannot ignore the length of Chinese Taipei's run of defeats. While there is potential for this match to be competitive at times, Vietnam should have enough quality to come through with a hard-earned win.

#1672. Everton targeting Iceland international as Thierno Barry alternative

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Everton could make signing a new centre-forward a priority in January after entering the season short of options in attack.

David Moyes needs additional firepower to strengthen his squad, and a promising Iceland international has reportedly emerged as a potential solution.

Real Sociedad striker Orri Oskarsson is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs, with Everton understood to be paying particularly close attention to his progress.

The 22-year-old has impressed in Spain, and the Toffees could explore a move as they look to address a key weakness in their squad.

According to TEAMtalk, Everton are among the clubs monitoring Oskarsson ahead of the January transfer window. Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Brentford are also reportedly tracking the Icelandic forward, meaning Moyes could face competition if Everton decide to pursue a deal.

Everton’s need for a striker has become increasingly apparent following their summer business. Beto departed for Fiorentina without a replacement arriving, leaving Thierno Barry as the club’s only recognised centre-forward. Attempts to sign Folarin Balogun from Monaco and Joshua Zirkzee from Manchester United also failed to produce a deal.

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1671. Chelsea targeting Trent Alexander-Arnold as surprise transfer opportunity emerges

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Chelsea could be preparing for a significant change at right-back as the club assess their options ahead of the upcoming transfer windows.

With uncertainty surrounding Malo Gusto’s future at Stamford Bridge, the Blues have reportedly identified an unexpected target who could bring considerable experience and creativity to their defence.

Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold has emerged as a potential option, with former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown suggesting the England international could be tempted by a move to west London if Chelsea decide to make an approach.

According to Football Insider, Chelsea are keeping tabs on Alexander-Arnold as questions continue over his role at Real Madrid. The 28-year-old has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter under Jose Mourinho, with competition for places limiting his opportunities.

Brown revealed that Chelsea are among the clubs monitoring the situation, telling Football Insider: “One name who I have heard in connection with a move to Chelsea is Trent Alexander-Arnold.”

He admitted the potential transfer had initially surprised him, adding: “It came as a bit of a surprise to me, to be honest, but he has fallen well down the pecking order at Real Madrid to the point where he’s now the second or even third choice.”

The former scout also questioned whether the defender currently fits into Mourinho’s plans, explaining:

“It appears Mourinho doesn’t rate him particularly in that right-back position, and he’s not the only one, because he’s been out in the cold for England as well.”

Despite those concerns, Brown believes Alexander-Arnold remains an attractive player because of his technical ability and reputation. Chelsea, meanwhile, have reportedly been assessing potential replacements for Gusto as they consider changes to their defensive options.

Brown added: “Alexander-Arnold is a talented footballer who has a very good skillset, but it is those weaknesses in his game that often raises concerns.”

He also suggested that Chelsea’s interest in high-profile players could make the move possible: “Chelsea, though, will always be keen on the possibility of signing a big-name player; it’s just what they do, so they’ll be keeping an eye on whether he does become available.”

The possibility of a return to Liverpool has also been discussed, but Brown believes Stamford Bridge could become a realistic destination if the defender decides to leave Spain.

#1670. Ex-Man United star Clayton Blackmore is forced to apologise for encouraging Mason Greenwood to 'come home to us' after winger beat Liverpool with Fenerbahce

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 13:06 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 13:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Former Manchester United footballer Clayton Blackmore has apologised after being criticised on social media for asking Mason Greenwood to 'come home' to Old Trafford.

Greenwood, 25, played a pivotal role for Fenerbahce during their 3-2 victory over Manchester United's archrivals Liverpool in the Champions League on Wednesday, scoring the Turkish giants' first-half equaliser.

The English forward broke through the ranks as a youngster at Manchester United and looked destined to become a key long-term player, but his career spiralled after he was arrested and charged in 2022 with suspected attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm.

Although those charges were subsequently dropped by the Crown Prosecution Service in February 2023, United decided Greenwood could not continue to ply his trade at Old Trafford after undertaking an internal six-month investigation.

Since his exit, which came after disgruntled Manchester United supporters groups heaped pressure on the club to cut ties with the forward, Greenwood has represented Spanish club Getafe on loan, French giants Marseille and Turkish side Fenerbahce, who he joined this summer for a reported €39million (£33.27million).

Blackmore, who played for Manchester United between 1982 and 1994, was met with backlash on Thursday after he heaped praise on Greenwood for his role in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool.

Mason Greenwood (centre) celebrates after scoring in Fenerbahce's 3-2 win over Liverpool

Former Man United star Clayton Blackmore pleaded for Grenwood to 'come home to us'

The 62-year-old Welshman apologised after his post was met with a furious backlash online

Greenwood's Manchester United career ended after he was charged with attempted rape, controlling and coercive behaviour and assault causing actual bodily harm in 2022

'Well done Mason Greenwood beating Liverpool. Come home to us please,' the Welshman, 62, posted on X.

Two hours later, after receiving a slew of disparaging comments on the platform, he said: 'Sorry I've offended anyone but I heard he had been cleared of any wrongdoing I apologise to everyone I've upset with my comments like I said I thought he had been cleared of everything and he’s had a baby with his girlfriend. Big sorry.'

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness that both Greenwood and Angel Gomes, another former English prodigy who was sold to Lille by Manchester United in 2020, no longer play for the club.

When the duo were both playing at Marseille last season, Blackmore said on X: 'Good to see Angel Gomez and Mason Greenwood score Marseille in first 26 mins. Sad they're not still at United.'

After landing himself in hot water with the post, he clarified to those commenting: 'Sorry I understand what you're saying but sometimes everything you hear is not always the truth why did his girlfriend stay with him I'm just looking at the football side.'

He later doubled down and wrote: 'Sorry didn't see or hear any of that I will do my home work next time just looking at it from the football side sorry if I've offended anyone especially his girlfriend and her family.'

While there was noisy resistance to Greenwood joining Marseille in the summer of 2025, he found no such opposition in Turkey, where one prominent journalist claimed 95 per cent of the population would not know or care about his past.

He didn't face any questions about the dropped charges or his public image in his first press conference and outside of brief post-match comments, has not conducted any interviews of note.

Greenwood has been hiding from the limelight a record signing would usually bask in, especially in the football-crazed city of Istanbul.

He found a home in a district called Sarıyer, a favourite among footballers, who largely live in gated communities.

Greenwood is said to count team-mates N'Golo Kante and Marco Asensio as neighbours and was seen in a rare online post after securing his new home, posing with the all-female team of estate agents who helped him with the purchase.

The former United starlet completed his move to Turkish giants Fenerbahce in the summer

Blackmore had previously come under fire for expressing his sadness at Greenwood leaving

Since the big-money move, Greenwood has only posted a handful of times on his Instagram profile, all of which were generic action shots after matches.

His latest offering came after Fenerbahce's stunning win over Liverpool, as he posted a gallery of photographs celebrating in the club's yellow and black jersey.

His partner, Harriet, 26, is also selective with how much she shares from their new life.

She only has four posts in total, with around 20 photos in each 'round-up', offering a glimpse into the high-life, though Greenwood himself only appears twice.

One of the images is of him looking exhausted in hospital at the birth of their second daughter in 2023 and another shows him holding hands with their eldest, Summer, who is three.

#1669. Manchester United targeting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in surprise January transfer move

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United could be forced to strengthen their attacking options in January after another injury setback involving Benjamin Sesko.

With Michael Carrick needing additional firepower to maintain competition for places up front, an experienced Premier League striker has reportedly emerged as a surprise target.

Leeds United forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin is among the names being considered by United’s recruitment team. However, attempting to sign a key player from one of their biggest rivals could prove extremely difficult.

According to The Athletic, Manchester United are exploring the January market for centre-forwards, with Calvert-Lewin one of the players under consideration.

The 29-year-old England international has reportedly been on United’s radar for some time, and recruitment staff are now assessing whether a potential transfer would be feasible when the window opens.

The interest comes amid concerns over Benjamin Sesko’s availability. The Slovenian striker is expected to miss an extended period with a shin injury, leaving Carrick with fewer recognised centre-forward options.

Calvert-Lewin has rebuilt his career since joining Leeds on a free transfer from Everton in 2025. His performances at Elland Road have attracted renewed attention, with the striker scoring 20 goals in 49 appearances for the club across all competitions.

He has also returned to England international contention following his improved form, making him an appealing option for United as they consider their attacking requirements.

However, there are significant obstacles. Leeds are reportedly keen to reward Calvert-Lewin with a new contract, despite his current agreement running until 2028. The club are also understood to be protective of a player who has become an important part of Daniel Farke’s side.

The rivalry between Leeds and Manchester United presents another major complication. A transfer between the clubs would attract considerable attention, and reports suggest the possibility of an agreement is currently remote.

Calvert-Lewin could offer United a different profile in attack, bringing physical presence, aerial ability and considerable Premier League experience. His availability could become particularly important if Sesko remains sidelined into the January window.

United have previously considered alternative centre-forward options, but the latest developments could encourage the recruitment department to widen its search. Calvert-Lewin’s experience in English football would potentially make him an attractive short-term solution.

Nevertheless, Leeds are unlikely to make negotiations straightforward. They have little reason to weaken their squad midway through the campaign, particularly by allowing an important player to join their historic rivals.

United must also consider whether pursuing Calvert-Lewin is realistic when other striker targets may be easier to acquire.

For now, the reported interest represents an option under consideration rather than an imminent transfer. Sesko’s injury has increased the urgency surrounding United’s search for attacking reinforcements, but persuading Leeds to sell their striker could prove a significant challenge.

#1667. Sunderland: Jules Ahoka’s incredible rise from Congolese second division to unlikely Chelsea hero

By Axel Clody | 09 Nov 2026 11:42

Jules Ahoka, a key figure in Sunderland’s victory over Chelsea on Sunday in the Premier League, embodies one of the most meteoric rises of his generation.

Introduced for Sunderland as early as the fourth minute after captain Granit Xhaka went off injured, Ahoka shone against Chelsea on Sunday in the 10th round of the Premier League season (1-0 win).

Thanks to his non-stop work, the versatile 20-year-old defensive midfielder was named man of the match. It was a prize as rewarding as it was symbolic for a player who was playing on sand just two years ago.

❤️ The dressing room reaction ? The Ahoka speech Your Player of the Match, Jules Ahoka ?? https://t.co/ha29otzcZ2

Sunderland signed Ahoka at the end of August from Royal Antwerp for £8.5m (€10m). That is more than 44 times the fee for his move from his youth club AC Normands Sport in the Congolese second division a year ago (£191,000 according to estimates from the specialist website Transfermarkt).

Before that, the 1.90m giant had shone in the AFCON Under-20 qualifiers that ended with DR Congo qualifying after a 12-year wait. Royal Antwerp won the race for his signature ahead of around ten suitors who were attracted by his work rate in midfield.

The Belgian club managed to keep him despite strong interest from Chelsea, who initially wanted to loan him to Strasbourg, another club in the BlueCo group, after his notable performances for DR Congo at the Maurice Revello Tournament with the captain’s armband on his bicep.

He needed only two games with the first team at Royal Antwerp to convince Sunderland to take a gamble on his profile. Welcomed by compatriot Noah Sadiki, he is represented by the same agent as Oscar Kabwit.

A DR Congo Under-23 international (six caps, two goals), Ahoka was not selected by manager Sebastien Desabre for the senior 2027 AFCON qualifiers, apparently judged too raw. If he continues on his current path, he could receive his first call-up in the next squad list.

#1664. Bradford City vs York City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 09 Nov 2026 11:54, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 11:57

Northern Group C leaders Bradford City welcome bottom-placed York City to Valley Parade on Tuesday night for their third and final EFL Trophy group fixture, with both sides already knowing their fate in the competition.

The Bantams head into the clash on the back of an emphatic 7-0 victory over Marine in the FA Cup, while the Minstermen also enjoyed a convincing win of their own after thrashing Northampton Town 4-0.

Following Graham Alexander's departure earlier this season to take charge of Championship side Preston North End, Bradford City turned to Michael Duff as their new head coach, in what was a potential gamble given that he had been relieved of his duties at Wycombe Wanderers just a few weeks earlier.

Duff inherited a side sitting second in the division after eight matches, but the Bantams have since endured an inconsistent spell, with just one win from their last six league games leaving them outside the playoff places.

However, they do have a game in hand on four of the top six and could climb back into fourth with a victory.

Bradford brought October to a disappointing close with a West Yorkshire derby against league leaders Huddersfield Town, suffering a comfortable 3-0 defeat that also saw captain Antoni Sarcevic sent off.

After that Halloween setback, Duff's side turned their attention to the FA Cup, where they faced National League North outfit Marine and ran out emphatic 7-0 winners.

Nick Powell and Adam Phillips both scored twice, while Will Swan, George Lapslie and Matthew Pennington also found the net as the Bantams avoided a potential cup upset and recorded their biggest victory of the season.

As for York City, they enjoyed a dramatic end to last season, securing promotion to League Two in the dying moments of their campaign thanks to a Josh Stones goal in the 13th minute of stoppage time against title rivals Rochdale.

Their promotion ended a 10-year absence from the English Football League and came under the guidance of Stuart Maynard, who was surprisingly replaced by Scott Lindsey over the summer, much to the frustration of York supporters.

Despite the unexpected appointment, the former Crawley boss has made a positive start to life in the fourth tier, with five wins, five draws and four defeats keeping the Minstermen in the playoff places.

However, York have been unable to carry their encouraging league form into the EFL Trophy and sit bottom of the group after successive defeats, knowing that even a victory on Tuesday will not change their fate in the competition.

The Minstermen did enjoy a much better afternoon in the FA Cup on Saturday, though, progressing to the second round with a 4-0 victory over Northampton Town in a match where they took the lead after just 10 seconds.

With league football remaining the main priority and both sides already knowing their fate in the EFL Trophy, the two managers are likely to make several changes to their starting lineups.

Jon McCracken is expected to make way for Cameron Dawson in goal, while Harry Cartwright could also be recalled to the starting XI.

Bobby Pointon is set to miss out after picking up an early injury on Saturday, while Lapslie could come into the side from the start after scoring against Marine. He will be joined on the sidelines by Josh Neufville, however.

Lindsey is expected to bring George Sykes-Kenworthy back into the fold, while Jack Hunt could also return to the back four.

Vice-captain Ollie Pearce is likely to be rested after scoring twice in the FA Cup, with Afolabi Akinyemi among the leading candidates to come into the side up front.

Dawson; Welch, Matthews, Gillesphey; Ibbitson, Morgan, Cartwright, O'Keeffe; Lapslie, Humphrys, Swan

Sykes-Kenworthy; J. Hunt, Palmer, McArthur; Felix, Stiver, Read, Medley; Malcolm, Akinyemi, Maguire

Although both sides have enjoyed positive spells in their respective leagues, Bradford are competing a division above York and we expect that difference in quality to be evident on Tuesday night.

We are backing the Bantams to make it two cup victories in the space of four days and ahead into the EFL Trophy knockout stages with a 2-0 win at Valley Parade.

Published: 13:29 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 17:28 EST, 5 November 2026

Newcastle United star Amar Dedic was at the centre of a major police operation after he was spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot – with at least SIX patrol cars involved in the search for the £30million defender.

The Bosnia international sparked alarm when a concerned member of the public reported seeing him and a friend walking with the weapon near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the area in Harlow Hill, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were finally intercepted around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Sources have described the dramatic swoop on Dedic's vehicle before officers searched the car and seized a bow and arrows, with the 24-year-old questioned about his activities.

In a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance.

After speaking to the two men, officers were satisfied there was no threat to the public, with police subsequently stating that the equipment was believed to have been intended for recreational use.

Amar Dedic played in Newcastle's 1-0 defeat by Everton on Monday evening

Dedic was spotted with a crossbow off Military Road, the 61-mile B6318 in Northumberland

However, enquiries remain ongoing into the incident, which happened on Wednesday afternoon. It is understood that Dedic and his friend had fired some arrows while in the countryside, although it remains unclear what they were aiming at. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in the UK.

Dedic joined Newcastle from Benfica during the summer and has impressed at right back despite the club's difficult start to the season.

Daily Mail Sport understands he will not face disciplinary action from Newcastle over the incident, although there is a feeling that the player was naive to believe he could walk around the countryside carrying such weaponry.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson said: 'Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

'Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Enquiries are ongoing.'

Dedic is expected to be available for Saturday's Premier League trip to Fulham, where Newcastle will attempt to halt a run of four defeats in five matches across all competitions.

His opponent today will be Morten Frendrup, someone that Milan have been repeatedly linked with over the years. The Dane remains Genoa’s metronome in midfield, and the shield in front of the back three.

Summer signing Milutin Osmajić has been Genoa’s main threat in quite a low-scoring side, with four goals to his name in Serie A. He is keeping Lorenzo Colombo out of the side, though the Italian has provided a couple of assists for the Montenegrin when they have been fielded together in a front two.

After a disastrous performance against Ferencvaros, Koni De Winter will be hoping for a much better outing this afternoon. The Belgian has been in the headlines for rejecting a Belgium call-up meaning he will stay over the break, and he will aim to channel that same display against Marcus Thuram in the derby.

In addition to Rabiot, the other player to establish himself as a major threat for Milan is Diego Moreira. The Belgian has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for the Rossoneri, and that came after a bit of a slow start too. He was decisive in the derby, with two assists and a beautiful free-kick goal.

He is expected to have quite a free-ranging role on the right, but what will be very important is getting players around Goncalo Ramos to try and unlock the Portuguese. So, Moreira will likely come up against the left-sided centre-back Johan Vasquez, someone who has become a mainstay in the Genoa side having entered his fifth season there. He does have three bookings in his first nine games, so that could be something to target.

Speaking of Goncalo Ramos, the concerns about his scoring form (or lack thereof) are beginning to grow into full-blown panic. He still has only two Serie A goals to his name so far, one of which was a penalty, and his overall involvement in the Rossoneri’s attacking play seems to be fluctuating between very little and non-existent.

Amorim and the team must get him firing, or it will continue to look like €70m+ spent very badly. Today will not be an easy duel for the former PSG man either as he faces Leo Ostigard, someone who will be well up for the physical battle. As we have seen, Ramos can get frustrated when he faces players who man-mark him, so he will have to be smart and sharp with his movement, ideally getting some more service too.

With an honourable mention going to Christian Pulisic vs. Alessandro Marcandalli, we had to end by mentioning Stephan El Shaarawy. He scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for Milan, becoming a fan favourite during his time. The winger has also become the main creative force for the Grifone, having provided an assist in each of his last two league appearances.

Given his propensity to cut inside in order to create danger, both Mario Gila but especially Yunus Musah will have to watch the 34-year-old very closely indeed. Milan have been exposed in transition several times this season, and there is no doubt El Shaarawy would love to make a statement against his old club.
