Proposed source regions for the spread of Celtic under the four evaluated models are highlighted with a dashed circle. b, A timeline showing the demographic movements discussed throughout the study. Movements 1, 2 and 3 are labelled. c, A density plot showing the overlap of estimates for the divergence of Pre-Celtic, the emergence and dissolution of Proto-Celtic and the subsequent divergence of Goidelic and Brittonic (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Error bars are included in the density calculations. Studies that provide only a start or end date are presented with a fading error bar and not included in the density calculation. d, Published computational linguistic estimates for the divergence of Pre-Celtic from the nearest other Indo-European branch. Error bars represent the uncertainty of the computational methods, as presented in the respective studies. e, Published non-computational (archaeo-)linguistic estimates for the formation and fragmentation of Proto-Celtic. Error bars represent the uncertainty of the estimates, as presented in the respective studies. Studies that provide only a start or end time are presented with a fading error bar. f, Published computational linguistic estimates for the divergence of the post-Proto-Celtic Brittonic and Goidelic branches from each other (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Error bars represent the uncertainty of the computational methods, as presented in the respective studies. Uncropped versions of c–f can be found in Extended Data Fig. 1. Base maps in a were generated in R (v.4.2.3) using map_data(“world”) in ggplot2 (v.3.5.0.9000); geographic boundary data are derived from the public-domain Natural Earth 1:50 m dataset (https://www.naturalearthdata.com) through the R maps package (v.3.4.2.1).

Movement 1 aligns with the linguistic Bell Beaker model, which attributes the formation and spread of Celtic to Bronze Age Bell Beaker populations (roughly 4750–4500 to 4000–3800 bp). Under this model, movement 1 would represent the arrival of Celtic to the regions from which movements 2 and 3 occurred, with the later movements potentially reflecting the spread of a branch of Celtic. In the time following movement 1, we do not see an influx of Corded Ware-related or Yamnaya-related ancestry in the Bell Beaker region, suggesting Indo-European dialects in the region are Bell Beaker-mediated. If Celtic or its ancestral dialect arrived later, it probably did so with limited demographic movement.

Movement 2 is consistent with the view that maritime connectivity of the Atlantic Bronze Age drove the formation of Celtic, as proposed by the Celtic-from-the-West model. It is furthermore geographically consistent with a hypothetical spread of Celtic from France (and possibly northern Italy), as claimed by the Celtic-from-the-Centre model. However, the latter specifically claims a spread after 3000 bp, whereas this movement occurred during the previous millennium, resulting in a chronological mismatch.

Movement 3 aligns with the Celtic-from-the-East model. This model draws on archaeological evidence indicating a westward expansion of populations deriving from the Urnfield Culture from eastern central Europe into France and northeastern Spain50,51. We also note that, like movement 1, this movement affects all known Celtic-speaking areas of Europe. Archaeologically, the persistence of Knovíz-related ancestry into the Iron Age is consistent with the transition from the Late Urnfield to the Hallstatt Culture being seen as a reorganization of settlements rather than the arrival of a new population52 (Supplementary Note 6). In addition, under the Celtic-from-the-East model, the westward expansion of Hallstatt C (2750–2600 bp), from the Rhine into England and Ireland53,54, then provides an extra potential vector for the spread of Celtic varieties, that is, Brittonic and Goidelic, to Britain.

Finally, all linguistic models converge on a Late Iron Age eastward spread of Gaulish-related dialects during the La Tène period (2400–2200 bp)55, ultimately extending from France to northern Italy, central Europe and the Balkans. Consistent with previous studies35, we indeed detect subtle genetic shifts (Supplementary Figs. 1.10 and 1.54) suggestive of a movement from the west during this period. It should be noted, however, that this genetic signal is more subtle than that of movements 1–3, and thus needs further confirmation.

For the four linguistic models, we identify relevant movements based on overlapping geographical ranges and assess their compatibility with the linguistic date estimates (Extended Data Table 1). When evaluated against the demographic movements identified here, the Bell Beaker model and the Celtic-from-the-East model require the fewest independent population dispersals and the least reliance on auxiliary assumptions to account for the historically attested distribution of Celtic. Whereas the Celtic-from-the-West model can be aligned with movement 2, it also requires the prolonged maintenance of Celtic linguistic identity across regions undergoing substantial subsequent admixture (movement 3).

To further assess the feasibility of these movements as vectors for the spread of Celtic, linguistic dating provides an extra constraint. The underlying linguistic date estimates and associated literature are summarized in Supplementary Note 5, Supplementary Fig. 5.1 and Supplementary Table 5.1. A plausible population vector for the spread of Celtic must fall after the initial Pre-Celtic linguistic divergence from other Indo-European branches, allowing time for the shared innovations that define Proto-Celtic to accumulate and before the subsequent diversification into the attested Celtic branches (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Most estimates for the divergence of Pre-Celtic overlap at 5000–3500 bp, with the highest density between 4500 bp and 3800 bp (Extended Data Fig. 1b). Estimates for the subsequent formation and fragmentation of Proto-Celtic fall mostly between 3600 bp and 2800 bp, with the highest overlap between 3200 bp and 3000 bp (Extended Data Fig. 1c). Finally, the divergence time of the Goidelic and Brittonic Celtic branches from each other has most estimates overlapping between 3500 bp and 2000 bp, with the highest overlap at 2800–2500 bp (Extended Data Fig. 1d).

Only movement 3 falls within the bounds provided by most quantitative estimates (the divergence of Pre-Celtic and the divergence into Goidelic and Brittonic), while also coinciding with the highest overlap of the qualitative estimates for the formation and fragmentation of Proto-Celtic (Fig. 5 and Extended Data Table 1), supporting the Celtic-from-the-East model. By contrast, movement 1 overlaps with many estimates for the divergence of Pre-Celtic, and both movements 1 and 2 predate most estimates for the formation and fragmentation of Proto-Celtic (Fig. 5 and Extended Data Table 1).

Given the present sampling density and available linguistic date estimates, we find the Celtic-from-the-East model to be the most parsimonious of the four predefined scenarios evaluated here (Methods). This preference does not rest on an assumption that linguistic spread must mirror demographic processes, but reflects that alternative models require further, at-present untested mechanisms such as prolonged linguistic continuity across major demographic turnover. At the same time, we note that human history does not necessarily follow the most parsimonious trajectory9, and the partial support for other models may result from a more complex divergence and spread, which cannot be excluded based on genomic data. If Bell Beaker groups with Steppe ancestry indeed transmitted Indo-European language varieties, it is likely that a continuum of related dialects, including those ancestral to Celtic, Italic and Lusitanian, were spoken across the region after 4400 bp. With this view, it is plausible that the people of movements 2 and 3 retained a degree of mutual intelligibility with the local population of Britain. Thus, the spread of Celtic may have involved the diffusion of Celtic linguistic features rather than a complete replacement of local languages: a complexity invisible to parsimony approaches. Although our findings do not definitively establish the homeland of the Celtic languages, they do constrain the demographic processes through which their formation and diffusion may be modelled. As a result, any revised or newly proposed models for the spread of the Celtic languages will need to reconcile with the demographic patterns identified in this study.

The 578 new ancient individuals included in the analyses here are part of a larger dataset of 712 ancient shotgun-sequenced genomes32. Details on the sampling, data generation, quality checks, site description and detailed metadata can be found in that study32. In brief, ancient samples were visually identified as suitable for processing. Samples were drilled, predigested56, extracted17, built into libraries57,58 and sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 4000 and NovaSeq 6000 platforms. Sequenced reads were mapped against the human reference genome build 37 (hs37d5) and authenticated based on the length of reads, damage patterns, endogenous rates and presence of contamination. All samples with a genomic coverage greater than 0.1× were imputed, and close relatives identified using ngsRelate (v.2)59 were excluded for IBD-based analyses.

Genomes were imputed using Glimpse (v.1.1.1)60 against the 1000 Genomes v.5 phase 3 dataset61. Shared IBD segments were called using IBDseq (v.r1206)62 with default parameters. Segments with a logarithm-of-the-odds (LOD) score less than three and hotspot regions39 with excess sharing were excluded. A detailed description can be found in the accompanying paper32.

To identify fine-scale structure, we applied IBD mixture modelling39. The use of non-negative least squares modelling has been routinely applied using chromopainter chunks shared between ancient source and target sets63. However, recent studies have shown that using shared IBD segments between ancient individuals is effective at recovering fine-scale detail32,39. We relied on the dataset and IBD clustering from the accompanying paper32. The cluster IDs for all individuals included can be found in Supplementary Table 1.1. The 4,587 ancient individuals in the dataset were determined to be suitable for IBD mixture modelling on the basis of a series of filtering steps for genomic coverage (0.1× for shotgun-sequenced data, 1× for 1,240,000 capture data), average genotype probability for the 1,240,000 capture sites (0.9) and the removal of close relatives. The final dataset included 690,211 sites that intersected with the 1000 Genomes panel and the 1,240 K sites, pass the 1000 Genomes mappability mask and had an imputation INFO score greater than 0.5.

For each of the 4,587 ancient individuals in the dataset, a palette was created representing the proportion of sharing with all other clusters, and with the other individuals in their own cluster. The proportions were normalized by the number of individuals in each cluster. To account for the fact that the sharing within the individual’s own cluster has n − 1 individuals, sharing with all other clusters excludes one individual at random. As a result, clusters with a single individual do not contribute to other individuals’ palettes. All segments greater than 1 cM, with a LOD score greater than 3, that did not originate from a hotspot of IBD sharing39 were included in the palettes. IBD mixture modelling was then undertaken using these palettes, by modelling the target individual using non-negative least squares38, as described in ref. 39. Standard errors of the ancestry proportions were calculated using a weighted block jackknife, leaving out each chromosome.

A strength of this method is that target palettes are modelled as combinations of potential source palettes, meaning information from all other individuals in the dataset is incorporated into the modelling, rather than relying solely on the sharing of segments between the source and target individuals. When applied to densely sampled regions such as Holocene western Eurasia, sources and targets separated by 10,000 years continue to be modelled reliably32.

To understand the trends in ancestry through time, we performed spatiotemporal kriging (STAdmix, v.c72d845)64 to interpolate IBD mixture modelling results for points in time and space where genetic data are not available. For the ancestry of particular relevance for set C2 (Corded Ware-related, Bell Beaker-related and European Farmer-related), set C3 (British–Irish Neo.-related, Iberia–France Neo.-related, Italy Neo.-related and Anatolia BA-related) and set C4 (S. France–N. Iberia BA-related and Hungary–Serbia BA-related), we fit spatiotemporal variograms by means of a metric covariance model65.

qpAdm analyses were undertaken on the 690,211 sites of the dataset described above, using admixtools2 (ref. 66). Populations were placed into three sets: left_fixed, right_fixed or rotational (Supplementary Table 2.4). The ‘left_fixed’ population was included as a potential source in all qpAdm analyses. The ‘right_fixed’ population was included as outgroups in all analyses. In one population model, all ‘rotational’ populations were included as outgroups. For two population models, one ‘rotational’ population was placed together with the ‘left_fixed’ population as potential sources, and all others as outgroups, in all possible combinations. For three population models, two ‘rotational’ populations were placed together with the ‘left_fixed’ population as potential sources, and all others as outgroups, in all possible combinations.

In the present context, parsimony is understood as the minimization of independent population dispersals, chronological mismatches and auxiliary explanatory mechanisms (such as prolonged language persistence under repeated large-scale admixture) required to reconcile linguistic, archaeological and genomic evidence. Parsimony here functions as a comparative constraint on explanatory models rather than as an assumption about how prehistoric language spread must have occurred. Accordingly, parsimony is used here as a heuristic for model comparison rather than as a criterion of historical likelihood.

To evaluate whether a linguistic model is parsimonious with the genetic data, we assess whether a movement occurred in a direction and to a geographical extent consistent with the spread proposed by the linguistic model. In addition, we test whether the time of the movement is consistent with expectations based on linguistic dating. A plausible population vector for the spread of Celtic must fall after the initial Pre-Celtic linguistic divergence from other Indo-European branches, allowing time for the shared innovations that define Proto-Celtic to accumulate, and before the subsequent diversification into the attested Celtic branches.

The extent to which each model is consistent with the most relevant movement and further assumptions required to fit the model to the movement are detailed in Supplementary Table 1. The model that requires the fewest independent population movements, chronological mismatches and auxiliary assumptions is evaluated as most parsimonious.

#1619. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

De Winter: I wasn’t actually super impressed by him. Gila: I don’t like him leaving too much gap behind, but honestly his attacks look more polished than Pavlović’s. Moreira: not that good defensively, but offensively, my man is a demon. Modrić: Honestly, I think the recent adjustments of Amorim (or whatever one can call them), suit him a bit better. He looked more rejuvinated recently. #1618. Nicolo Tresoldi: Italy call-up “a possibility” as Roberto Mancini issues update amid Germany competition

By Oliver Thomas | 09 Nov 2026 16:38

Italy head coach Roberto Mancini has provided a fresh update on the national team’s hopes of persuading Nicolo Tresoldi to represent the Azzurri over Germany.

The 22-year-old Club Brugge star was born in Cagliari to an Italian father and Argentine mother of Italian descent before he moved to Germany at the age of 13 for his mother's work.

Tresoldi joined Hannover 96 at youth level before spending three years in the senior team between 2022 and 2025, making 80 first-team appearances.

The striker has since elevated his game to new heights in Belgium with Club Brugge, while he has represented Germany at Under-19 and Under-21 level, scoring 19 goals 35 appearances across all tournaments.

Tresoldi’s standout performances have sparked a dual international tug-of-war between Italy and Germany, and he is still undecided on his long-term allegiance.

However, Mancini is optimistic that Italy can secure Tresoldi’s services following a conversation he and Claudio Ranieri - the technical director of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) - had with the in-demand striker.

Speaking at a press conference on Monday ahead of Italy resuming their UEFA Nations League campaign this week, Mancini told reporters: “I have spoken to [Tresoldi], as has Ranieri. He needs to feel that he wants to play for Italy.

“Given that he was born in Italy and his father played for Italy [and won the European Under-21 Championship], I think there could be a possibility.

“Ultimately, it is the player who has to make the decision. He knows that we believe he could be important for us.”

Tresoldi has once again been called up to Germany’s Under-21 squad for the November international break ahead of friendly matches against Belgium and Croatia.

The next international break is scheduled for the end of March 2027, giving Tresoldi plenty of time to mull over whether he wished to represent Italy or Germany - now managed by Jurgen Klopp - at senior level.

Both Italy and Germany are understandably keen to win the race for Tresoldi, who has established himself as one of the most prolific strikers in Europe over the last 12 months or so.

Last season, Tresoldi inspired Club Brugge to their 20th Belgian Pro League title after scoring 13 goals in 30 matches to win the division’s Golden Boot award.

He has since carried his prolific form in the new campaign, netting 14 goals in 17 appearances across all competitions, including eight strikes in 11 league games.

Tresoldi is currently the joint second-top scorer in the Champions League with five goals in just four matches, including a memorable hat-trick in a thrilling 4-3 away victory over Inter Milan last month.

Known for his elite penalty-box movement and high-intensity pressing, Tresoldi is understood to have caught the attention of some of Europe’s biggest clubs, including Premier League champions Arsenal.

Manchester City, Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur have also been credited with an interest in Tresoldi, who is valued at €35m (£29.2m) by transfermarkt and is under contract at Club Brugge until June 2029.

By Carter White | 09 Nov 2026 16:54

Manchester United are reportedly interested in hiring Bayern Munich assistant Aaron Danks to help under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick.

The 20-time English champions are sitting in 18th position in the Premier League standings following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at the Theatre of Dreams on Sunday afternoon, when the hosts completed another Old Trafford comeback.

Patrick Dorgu's last-minute equaliser was celebrated with considerable vigour, however, Man Utd remain in a worrying situation near the foot of the table, winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight contests.

It appears that the Red Devils have a real fight on their hands to retain their Premier League status, with United legend Roy Keane criticising head coach Carrick following the eight-goal thriller against Villa.

With the Premier League now taking a two-week break for international action, Man Utd have some time to recovery and prepare for a crunch clash with arch rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester United's hierarchy are set for 'high-level discussions' during the international break, analysing the start to the season and laying out a plan for the months ahead.

The future of head coach Carrick will be a major talking point for sporting director Jason Wilcox and head of recruitment Christopher Vivell, who have been sounding out potential replacements recently.

Former Newcastle United and Bournemouth boss Eddie Howe is supposedly of interest to Wilcox, whilst ex-Germany and Bayern Munich coach Julian Nagelsmann is said to have caught the eye of recruiter Vivell.

However, there is a reality in which Man Utd choose to stick with current leader Carrick, who has stated that he expects to take charge of the squad past the international break, despite an awful start to 2026-27.

It is understood that the club's boardroom are eyeing up a swoop for Bayern assistant Danks, who would arrive at the Theatre of Dreams to provide support for Carrick in his time of desperate need.

Working together at Championship outfit Middlesbrough in the past, Carrick and Danks possess a good footballing relationship, with the Bayern Munich man having plenty to offer the wounded English giants.

That being said, the direction of Red Devils travel is unlikely to change too much without significant change - whether that be to the playing staff or the people pulling the strings in the boardroom.

There is no doubt that the majority of United supporters would prefer a clean break from Carrick's faltering plans, instead of an attempt to strengthen the 45-year-old's backroom ranks.

#1615. Jack Grealish is EXILED by Everton: Ex-England star is still being left out, confirms boss David Moyes, after boozy nights at pubs and karaoke

By HARRY BAMFORTH, LIVE SPORTS COVERAGE REPORTER

Published: 08:52 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 19:01 EST, 5 November 2026

David Moyes has confirmed that Jack Grealish will be absent for Everton's clash with Coventry City on Friday following disciplinary action last week - and said he may not even return after the international break.

The 31-year-old was dropped for back-to-back matches against Newcastle following a 'breach of club discipline' and will not be part of the Toffees' matchday squad for the third game on the spin tomorrow night.

'No, Jack is not available,' Moyes said on Thursday. 'I wouldn't give you the plan, but we will be working with Jack again soon.'

Moyes was then questioned by reporters whether the club and Grealish will mend their relationship over the upcoming international break, which is set to span two weeks.

'We'll see,' Moyes replied. 'We need to wait and see how things go.'

Asked if Grealish is currently training Moyes added: ‘I would rather not answer your question.’

Grealish, who has made seven appearances since rejoining Everton for a second season-long loan spell in the summer, has been exiled since failing to show up for a training session on Monday last week. It is understood staff struggled to make contact with the winger.

The Manchester City loanee has since returned to training but is yet to feature for the club since the punishment, having missed both the Carabao Cup 3-1 win over Newcastle and the Premier League victory over the Magpies on Monday.

Jack Grealish remains exiled by Everton - with the winger not available for their game on Friday

Grealish has missed Everton's passed two games after being disciplined for missing training

Grealish had made four successive starts before he missed Everton's 2-0 defeat by Arsenal on October 24 due to illness.

It is thought Moyes had reservations about re-signing Grealish this summer after similar issues last season and last week the manager made it clear that he backed the 'club decision' to discipline the once England international.

Moyes said: 'You probably know I'm not going to give any details, it is a club decision and I support that decision. It is something I don't want to speak too much about.

'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it. All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job.'

Grealish is reported to have had back-to-back nights out prior to the Toffees' defeat in north London.

The three-time Premier League winner attended the Pride of Britain awards at the Grosvenor House hotel in London on October 19 where he presented the Child of Courage award to 12-year-old Zac Howells.

He is then reported to have finished the night of celebration off at Bam Karaoke Box, a karaoke hotspot in Victoria, central London. According to the Sun, he stayed up until the early hours of the morning singing with his friends and enjoying the drinks on offer.

Grealish is reported to have gone on consecutive nights out after attending the Pride of Britain Awards on October 19

The next day, Grealish is believed to have returned to Cheshire, where he and many of his footballer friends live, to meet team-mates Jordan Pickford and Tyler Dibling at The Mauldeth pub in Wilmslow.

The trio, joined by Grealish's former City team-mate and captain Kyle Walker, where they watched Paris Saint-Germain's thrilling Champions League victory over Barcelona. A witness claimed to the Sun that they enjoyed a few drinks.

Without Grealish once again, Everton are seeking to secure a third win in a row when they come up against former Toffees boss Frank Lampard and his Coventry team.

Their only injury concern ahead of the fixture is Jarrad Branthwaite, who Moyes admitted they have been nursing since he hobbled off late on at St. James' Park with cramp.

The Scot was speaking ahead of his 592nd game in charge of Everton, which will see him draw level with Harry Catterick’s record of the most games managed for the club.

‘I got told about it a few weeks ago,’ said Moyes, who has overseen more than 1,200 games during his coaching career. ‘I didn’t realise I’d got that close.

‘Harry Catterick’s name has always been mentioned alongside Howard [Kendall’s] name. I’m very proud to be up there, to be spoken of in terms of games. I wish I had the trophies to go with what they had.’

Victory over Coventry could see Everton move into the top-four places ahead of the November international break.

‘I think there’s lots to be positive about because of how they [the players] have been doing generally,’ said Moyes. ‘I feel we could have been doing better had we not lost some players last summer. I think it would have kept us right in and amongst it.

‘I think all you can try to do is get as many wins as you can and perform as well as we have. I think the players, in the main, have had good moments in games.’

Key to Everton’s form has been the goals of Thierno Barry. The 24-year-old has netted eight this term, already as many as he managed in his first season at the club.

Asked about the striker’s improvement, Moyes said: ‘I think the first thing is, he is settling down. We took a bit of an early gamble on buying Thierno and maybe knew he wouldn’t be right, right away. That’s been the case.

‘[Erling] Haaland should be worried that he’s just behind him now,’ he joked. ‘He has to be careful, Thierno is on his back.

‘Let’s hope he can keep scoring for us. He keeps trying to improve and I hope he can do that.’

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 17:59

Manchester United are reportedly huge admirers of Nottingham Forest's Murillo and could make a move for the centre-back during next summer's transfer window.

#1613. Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”

"We need to help them, not to rely everything on them" Xabi Alonso speaking about Chelsea's 'special' front three 🔵 pic.twitter.com/JnSBoNexF4

"Arsenal DON'T win the league if they have Ramsdale and not Raya" 🧤@Carra23 and @GNev2 think that upgrading the goalkeeper position could be the 'last piece' for Chelsea 🧩 pic.twitter.com/UBzMCFmxpp

"You can see in his eyes, he's ready to prove people wrong""Best player on the pitch by a mile" 👏Morgan Rogers reacts to his debut and the performance of Cole Palmer pic.twitter.com/M7JKk1MQ8U

"How ready are you?""Did you not watch the game?" 😅Cole Palmer says he is 'hungry' and ready to get back to his best! pic.twitter.com/xpg5zJl9k0

2 - Cole Palmer tonight vs Fulham:1 goal1 assist5 dribbles completed5 shots3 chances created7 ball recoveries10 duels wonHe was only the second player on record since 2006-07 to record all of these numbers in a Premier League game.Cold. pic.twitter.com/uW4YPeHNnD

“There were things to really like. On paper, that front three [for Chelsea] is sensational. It really is. It looked it in the game. I think Joao Pedro is fantastic. [Morgan] Rogers’ first game, what a start. But when you think of him, [Cole] Palmer and Pedro; that is as good as anything in the Premier League right now.

“But I do think concerns defensively. They conceded a couple of goals and you look at the goalkeeper. They have to sort the goalkeeper issue out because it is going to come back to haunt them this season, as it did tonight.”

“The attacking play, Cole Palmer was sensational. If you talk about Cole Palmer getting back to his best you have got a £120m-£125m player there. [Morgan] Rogers getting a goal. Those two being electric with Joao Pedro up front. The front three were brilliant tonight. One of the best things I have seen this weekend.

“They have added an experience player at centre-back, centre midfield and centre forward. I do not know if Emi Martinez is available or not but someone like that needs to come in at Chelsea, because that will undermine everything they do. The positives for Fulham came from the encouragement [Robert] Sanchez gave them with the goals. The goals were both mistakes. It is a problem.”

Possession: Fulham 61%-39% ChelseaShots: 14-18Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 6-4Touches in opposition box: 24-38

The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

Pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

Palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

Fulham make an attacking alteration as Muniz replaces Robinson

That is a huge, huge chance for Fulham to equalise. Robinson is played in behind the Chelsea defence with a long ball in behind and Sanchez is in no-man’s land out of his goal. Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. He then cuts inside onto his right, beating Lacroix with ease, and nearly beats Sanchez at his near post but his shot goes inches wide.

This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. Another poor piece of goalkeeping from Sanchez.

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

All members of Chelsea’s starting front three have got on the scoresheet tonight and Palmer also has an assist to his name.

Chelsea come close to a fourth as Hato squares it for Rogers inside the Fulham box but Robinson nips in just in front to clear.

He came close to scoring moments ago and now he does get on the scoresheet. Pedro gets onto the end of a flicked-on header by Rogers near halfway and drives into the Fulham half. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

Palmer does brilliantly down Chelsea’s right to skip past a number of defenders and moves into the Fulham penalty area. He opens up his body and curls one towards the far corner. He is adamant that there is a deflection but a goal kick is given. Replays show Palmer may have had a point.

Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

Forest are in talks with Chelsea over a potential loan deal for the forward after he was made available at Stamford Bridge and not included in their opening-day squad against Fulham.

Negotiations are ongoing, but Delap fits the profile of striker Forest are prioritising and is a long-term target for both the club and Glasner from his spell at Crystal Palace.

Possession: Fulham 60%-40% ChelseaShots: 7-13Shots on target: 2-5Corners: 4-3Touches in opposition box: 16-18

An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

The British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from new signings.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

Chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Good strike from King but terrible keeping from Sanchez.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

King does brilliantly to drive down Fulham’s right and flashes a dangerous ball across the six-yard box but none of his teammates are on hand to meet the cross.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. It looks like it should be a fairly routine save for Sanchez but the Chelsea keeper looks uncomfortable and pushes it behind for a corner. The delivery comes to the near post and King, who lays it off the edge of the box. It comes to Palacios, who cannot guide his effort on target.

Chelsea started this game well but have lost control and are asking for trouble. The latest example sees Sanchez take too long to clear and he accidentally allows the ball to go out before clearing to gift Fulham a corner. Bobb’s delivery is headed away at the near post by James.

That is strong one-vs-one defending from Bassey. Palmer lifts the ball over the top to pick out the run of Pedro, who is dispossessed inside the Fulham box by Bassey.

Moments later, Lavia flies into a reckless challenge on Bassey and is booked. Lavia looks stunned at that decision but he is perhaps on the fortunate side that VAR did not advise the referee to have a further look at that on the screen. Lavia was out of control and could have easily been in more trouble. Two Chelsea players already into the book and were a little bit lucky.

Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is in trouble. Could Chelsea go down to 10 men early? He loses possession poorly inside his own half and then resorts to hacking Bobb down with a nasty challenge. Was Colwill the last man and could Bobb have gone racing in on goal? Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

How do Alvaro Arbeloa and his Fulham side react now they are a goal down early?

With their first attack of the Xabi Alonso era, Chelsea hit the front inside the opening minute of this west London derby. Lacroix’s header from halfway finds Palmer, who plays it into the path of Pedro. The Brazilian, fresh from signing a new deal at the club, takes it in his stride and, from inside the Fulham penalty area, lifts it over Leno and into the far corner. A fine finish from Pedro and Alonso has the perfect start.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

Could Joao Pedro be the man to finally lift the curse of the number nine shirt at Chelsea? Liam Delap tried and failed last season. Pedro has taken it this term and has started like a train with that early goal. Pedro has also been prolific in pre-season and has been widely tipped to be one of the Premier League’s top scorers.

Before we get going, we take a moment to remember the great Kevin Keegan, who managed Fulham in the late 1990s.

We are under way at Craven Cottage in the final game on this opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Alvaro Arbeloa is out on the pitch for the first time in the Premier League. A friendly if not rapturous welcome from the home fans. He’s rolled his sleeves up and he’s ready to go - literally, his skinny fit jacket has sleeves rolled up tight. It looks quite uncomfortable.

It might be a new season and a new manager, but Chelsea are still doing their pre-match huddle. Fortunately, it was nowhere near the referee or the centre circle. It seemed to be captain Reece James doing all the talking.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Craven Cottage and we are moments away from kick-off in this west London derby. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up tonight:

Fulham: Leno; Castagne, Cuenca, Bassey, Robinson, King, Berge, Iwobi; Bobb, Garcia, Palacios.Substitutes: Lecomte, De Gougerolles, Tete, Reed, Charles, Sessegnon, Kevin, Smith Rowe, Muniz.

Chelsea: Sanchez; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Gusto, Lavia, James, Hato; Palmer, Pedro, Rogers.Substitutes: Penders, Chavarria, Barco, Enzo, Neto, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck, Quenda.

The boos for Fernandez from the Fulham fans got a lot louder when the players stepped on the pitch. Some people chanted something rather nasty beginning with ‘w’ as well.

There were a few boos from the Fulham fans when Enzo Fernandez’s name was read out ahead of kick-off. Clearly the England fans at Craven Cottage haven’t forgotten what happened against Argentina. Fernandez was booed by some Chelsea supporters in pre-season, but there were no loud jeers from the away end during the team announcements.

“During the week they had a few setbacks. With Moises [Caicedo], and with any [player], we do not want to take too much risk. They were not ready to play tonight. We need to go week-by-week but for tonight they were not ready.”

Chelsea certainly have an army of staff. I just counted 13 staff members helping the players through their warm-up. One of them is the new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee, who is carrying around a clipboard, presumably with all his set-piece tricks on it. Culture guru Willi Isa is also out there, as is former interim manager Calum McFarlane.

"The day to day culture that we want to build, they will play an important role" 📈Xabi Alonso explains his choice to join Chelsea and the importance of signings like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0koZ7ZyYYx

Chelsea’s £117m man Morgan Rogers has just run out for his warm up ahead of his competitive debut for the club. He’s kept in close contact with his best mate Cole Palmer, going through a few passing drills and doing a few keepy-ups. He looks relaxed so far.

"You NEED goals if you want to win games" ⚽️New Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa speaks about the losses of Harry Wilson and Raul Jimenez and the addition of Gonzalo Garcia 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/tbBujmljxm

The most interesting piece of Chelsea team news is that there is no Enzo Fernandez in the starting line-up, despite the surprise absence of Moises Caicedo. Instead, Romeo Lavia will partner Reece James in the centre of midfield, with Caicedo presumably injured. There is still an expectation that Manchester City will bid for Fernandez before the transfer window shuts, but the Argentine is on the substitutes’ bench. As expected, there is no place in the Chelsea squad for Nico Jackson and Liam Delap, both of whom have not travelled and are expected to leave Stamford Bridge. Aston Villa remain favourites to land Jackson, although Atletico Madrid have been showing an interest. Nottingham Forest are leading the race for Delap.

No more excuses. No more jam tomorrow. It is time for Chelsea to fight for the Premier League title this season. Anything else should be deemed a disappointment.

This is Chelsea version 3.0 under BlueCo, who bought the club four years ago. First there was Todd Boehly’s trolley dash, then came Behdad Eghbali’s youth club. This summer the focus has been on being Premier League-ready.

Off the pitch, the timing might be right for Boehly to be discussing the sale of his shares to Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital. But on it, Chelsea look better equipped to re-enter the title conversation than at any point in the BlueCo era.

Let's get it.#CFC | #FULCHE pic.twitter.com/G2M8LknNgV

Monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#1612. Amorim gets his response: Instant reaction to Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

Stefano recorded his reaction to AC Milan’s win against Genoa straight after the full-time whistle, highlighting the importance of the result.

There was some anxiety heading into today’s game, given the confidence beating earlier this week and the recent form of Genoa. However, within just 20 minutes, Milan found themselves two goals to the good and were able to control most of the game from there on.

#1611. Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression1,2, whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient −1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.

a, Schematic of the dual-luciferase reporters used to quantify +1 and −1 ribosomal frameshifting activity, together with the corresponding control constructs. b, Histogram showing the distribution of read counts for the +1 and −1 frame reporter libraries. c, Nucleotide frequency across the randomized 10-nt insert sequences in the reporter library. d, Quantification of +1 frameshifting activity across multiple cancer cell lines using 10-nt randomized dual-luciferase reporters. “Ctrl” denotes a control reporter lacking an inserted sequence. e, Quantification of −1 frameshifting activity across multiple cancer cell lines using 6-nt randomized dual-luciferase reporters. “Ctrl” denotes a control reporter lacking an inserted sequence. f, Quantification of frameshifting activity for positive-control constructs transfected into HEK293T cells using dual-luciferase reporters containing known frameshifting elements. g, Correlation between out-of-frame rates estimated from Ribo-seq and mean frameshifting activities measured by dual-luciferase reporters in f. h, Heatmap showing in-frame rates for codon pairs across the Ribo-seq dataset. i, Aggregation plots displaying in-frame rates and −1 frame rates before and after codon pairs. “Low” indicates the bottom 10% of codon pairs (n = 372 pairs). “Low-Rev”: codon pairs identical to those in the “Low” group, but with the order of the two codons reversed. j, Scatter plot showing the correlation between Fluc/Rluc ratios and Ribo-seq-derived −1-frame rates. 29 codon pairs were randomly selected, inserted into dual-luciferase reporters and quantified for frameshifting activity. In d–e, data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples. In f–g, data are mean ± SEM; n = 4 biologically independent samples. In g and j, Pearson’s correlation coefficients were calculated and two-sided P values are shown.

a, Frame analysis of Ribo-seq, with the majority of datasets showing in-frame rate higher than 70%. b, Frameshifting activity of individual codon pairs in HCT116 cells. A single codon pair was inserted between Rluc and Fluc in the dual-luciferase reporter, with Fluc placed in the −1 frame relative to Rluc. Numbers on the bars refer to average values (%) of the three replicates. Although a single codon pair is sufficient to induce significant frameshifting signals in HCT116 cells, to increase the detectable frameshifting signal in other cells and thereby facilitate analysis of both regulatory mechanisms and anti-tumour effects, we used 5× tandem repeats of the frameshifting motif in this study. c, Comparison of frameshifting activity using different repeat numbers of the frameshifting motif. For the 3×, 5× and 10× constructs, adjacent motifs were separated by a CCC codon. CCC was selected because cytosine-rich spacer sequences are less likely than A-, T- or G-rich spacers to generate premature stop codons (TAA, TAG or TGA) with adjacent sequences, thereby minimizing unintended effects on reporter expression. Numbers on the bars refer to average values (%) of the three replicates. d, Comparison of frameshifting activity when repeated frameshifting motifs were separated by different synonymous proline codons. CCC produced the lowest frameshifting activity, whereas CCG produced the highest. Because CCG is a relatively rare proline codon (RSCU = 0.46) compared with CCC (RSCU = 1.3), these results suggest that spacer codon usage can influence motif activity. In the AGAACG construct separated by CCT, the spacer introduces a − 1 frame stop codon (TAG), thereby terminating −1 frame translation. e, Frameshifting activity in HEK293T and HCT116 cells stably expressing the indicated 5× motif reporter constructs. f, Box plot comparing out-of-frame translation in the +1 and −1 frames between codon pairs with high in-frame rates (top 10%, n = 372 pairs) and low in-frame rates (bottom 10%, n = 372 pairs). Out-of-frame rates are shown relative to the high in-frame group to correct for basal differences in footprint counts across reading frames. g, Comparison of +1 and −1 frameshifting activity in HCT116, PANC-1 and A549 cells. In HCT116 and PANC-1 cells, the frameshifting-prone codon pairs AGAACG and ACGAGA exhibited significantly higher −1 frameshifting activity than the frameshifting-negative control pair CCAAGT, whereas +1 frameshifting at these pairs was low and comparable to CCAAGT. By contrast, in A549 cells, −1 frameshifting was lower than in HCT116 and PANC-1 cells, whereas +1 frameshifting was higher, reaching 2.7% for AGAACG and 1.1% for ACGAGA. h, Analysis as in g using a reporter containing codon pair GGATCC, which showed minimal −1 frameshifting but higher +1 frameshifting. The same CCAAGT control data shown in g are replotted here using a narrower y-axis scale for comparison. In b–e, g and h, data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples. In f, boxes show the median and 25th–75th percentiles; whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5× the interquartile range, with outliers shown individually.

a, Fluc/Rluc ratios and corresponding western blots for selected codon pairs tested in HEK293T cells. “uStop” indicates reporters containing a stop codon upstream of the inserted sequence, which terminates translating ribosomes in the upstream region. “dStop” indicates reporters containing a stop codon immediately downstream of the inserted sequence, which terminates −1 frame translation. b, Schematic of the dual-luciferase reporter system used to test for alternative translation initiation or cryptic promoter activity, together with the expected Fluc/Rluc ratios. If Fluc expression were driven by alternative initiation or a cryptic promoter, Fluc activity in the control reporter would be comparable to that in reporters containing the insert. In this study, control reporters showed minimal Fluc activity, suggesting that the observed out-of-frame translation is unlikely to be attributable to spurious initiation or cryptic promoter activity. c, Schematic illustrating potential alternative splicing in the dual-luciferase reporter and the corresponding expected Fluc/Rluc ratios. If Fluc expression resulted from alternative splicing, Fluc activity would be expected to remain detectable in the +1 frame, uStop and dStop reporters, rather than being restricted to the −1 frame reporter. However, these control reporters showed minimal Fluc activity, arguing against alternative splicing as a major contributor. d, RT-PCR analysis of mRNA from dual-luciferase reporters designed to detect aberrant splicing induced by the inserted sequences. Amplified products were resolved by agarose gel electrophoresis and validated by Sanger sequencing. No novel splice junctions were detected near the insertion site, supporting the conclusion that the inserts do not generate new splice donor or acceptor sites. e, Frameshifting activity measured using in vitro-transcribed mRNA reporters. The indicated constructs were transcribed into mRNAs by in vitro transcription and transfected into the indicated cells. Luciferase activity was analysed as for plasmid-based reporters. f, Comparison of frameshifting activity between breast cancer cell lines MDA-MB-231, BT20 and SK-BR-3, and the non-cancerous breast epithelial cell line MCF10A. Numbers on the bars refer to average values (%) of the three replicates. g, Comparison of frameshifting activity between lung cancer cell lines A549, HCC827, and the non-cancerous cell line BEAS-2B. Numbers on the bars refer to average values (%) of the three replicates. h, Comparison of frameshifting activity between liver cancer cell lines Huh-7, HepG2, and the non-cancerous cell line THLE-2. Numbers on the bars refer to average values (%) of the three replicates. In a, e–h, data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples; y-axis scales match that for HCT116 cells in Fig. 1g. In a, f–h, western blots were performed once, with concordant findings observed in additional cell lines and related experiments. In d, the experiment was performed once.

a, Schematic of the construct used to detect frameshift-derived proteins. The Flag tag is positioned in the −1 reading frame immediately downstream of the AGAACG codons. Note that the Flag sequence lacks a stop codon in either the in-frame or out-of-frame, avoiding premature termination caused by Flag sequence. b, Western blots showing product of frameshifting. The frameshifting codon pair AGAACG within the coding sequence is indicated by a red slash. Coding region is indicated by a blue frame. Lanes 1-4: CCD841, HCT116, SW480, and Caco2 cells without MG132 treatment. Lanes 5-8: CCD841, HCT116, SW480, and Caco2 cells treated with MG132. The numbers in parentheses indicate the length of CDS (nt), and the position of the frameshifting motif within CDS.

a, Comparison of ribosome density between mRNAs with or without frameshifting codon pairs. “Codon pairs” denotes the seven frameshifting-positive pairs in Fig. 1. b–d, Same as a, showing mRNA expression, translation efficiency and protein abundance, respectively. e, mRNA stability of transcripts with or without frameshifting pairs in CCD841 and HCT116 cells. f, Gene Ontology pathways enriched among mRNAs containing frameshifting pairs. g,h, RT-qPCR analysis of stability of frameshifting-bearing transcripts TXLNA and PRDX3 after UPF1 knockdown. i, Steady-state abundance of dual-luciferase reporter mRNAs. GFP, expressed in the opposite orientation from the same plasmid, served as an internal control for transfection efficiency. PTC-control contains an NMD-positive element obtained from a previous study75. j–m, Reporter mRNA stability after UPF1 knockdown for PTC-control (j), the frameshifting-negative pair CCAAGT (k), ACGAGA (l) and AGAACG (m). Replacing the frameshifting motif with the canonical NMD-positive element rendered the reporter NMD-sensitive, consistent with sequence-context-dependent modulation of NMD efficiency around premature termination codons75. n–q, Expression of NMD components and ZNF598 in colorectal cancer versus CCD841 cells (n), breast cancer versus MCF10A cells (o), lung cancer versus BEAS-2B cells (p), and liver cancer versus THLE-2 cells (q). In a–e, boxes show the median and 25th–75th percentiles; whiskers extend to the most extreme values within 1.5× the interquartile range, with outliers shown individually. n = 10,634, 3,478, 996, 333, 127 and 83 transcripts for the 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and ≥5 motif groups, respectively. In g, h and j–m, data are mean ± s.d.; P values correspond to comparisons at the final time point using a two-sided unpaired t-test; n = 3 biologically independent samples. In i, data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples. In n–q, western blots show three biologically independent samples per cell line.

#1610. Michael Carrick future: Review 'ongoing' at Man United - what will be the outcome?

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 18:27

Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox is reportedly leading the review into Michael Carrick's future at Old Trafford.

A disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, with the team winning just one of their first 10 league games of the season.

Man United did manage to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League last week, though, before twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, and the season has now been interrupted by an international break.

There is huge uncertainty when it comes to Carrick's future, with the sporting department at Old Trafford now reviewing the head coach's position.

According to The Guardian, Wilcox is leading the review, with chief executive Omar Berrada also being consulted, before a recommendation is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carrick was expected to be sacked by Man United off the back of the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25, but he was allegedly given three games to save his job - the trip to Chelsea in the Premier League, followed by the games against Roma and Villa.

It is understood that Eddie Howe is Wilcox's number one choice to replace Carrick, should a change be made, but that is not thought to be a view universally shared by the decision-makers.

Man United are next in action at Anfield on November 22, facing Liverpool in the Premier League, before facing Sporting Lisbon away from home in the Champions League.

November will then conclude with a home league game against Brentford.

"We’re in November. I don’t like the situation we’re in or the results we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it. We haven’t won enough games but I expect to move forward," Carrick told Sky Sports News after the draw with Villa.

"We’ll keep working on the things we’ve been working on, and tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

The positions of both Wilcox and Berrada have also been called into question due to Man United's ongoing struggles, and the pair are facing uncertain futures.

There remain calls from the club's supporters for the Glazer family to sell their share of the 20-time English champions, but there are no indications at this stage that will occur.

As it stands, Carrick is likely to remain in charge of Man United for the Liverpool game, with the Englishman still being backed despite the team's struggles this season.
