#1591. Woltemade involved in both goals but VAR denies Lucumí as Juventus draw 2-2 with Rennes

Nick Woltemade created Juventus's opener and scored their equaliser, but Jhon Lucumí's late winner against Rennes was ruled out for offside. The draw in Turin moves Spalletti's side to seven points in the Europa League league phase ahead of Sunday's trip to Lecce.

Juventus came within a VAR decision of beating Rennes at the Allianz Stadium on Thursday 22 October. Jhon Lucumí found the net in the 90th minute. Referee Morten Krogh studied the pitchside monitor and disallowed the goal for offside. Eight minutes of stoppage time followed, and the match finished 2-2.

Nick Woltemade was central to both Juventus goals. Spalletti’s side now sit on seven points after three league-phase matches. They had lost 0-3 to Lazio in their previous game.

Zeki Çelik put Juventus ahead in the fifth minute from Woltemade’s pass. Mousa Al-Tamari equalised in the 15th minute, set up by Bryan Reynolds. Federico Gatti was booked in the 19th minute for stopping the Rennes goalkeeper from taking a quick clearance.

Weston McKennie hit the post at around the half-hour mark with the score still level. Rennes then won a penalty when Douglas Luiz was penalised for handball. Boulaye Dia converted it in the 43rd minute, and the visitors led 1-2 at the break. Çelik, the scorer of the opener, went off injured after 45 minutes. Al-Tamari earned the match’s top rating from the data provider, 8.2.

The equaliser came from the spot. Reynolds blocked a Nico González header with his arm away from his body, and VAR upheld the award. Woltemade scored the penalty in the 67th minute. He finished with seven shots and two key passes.

Juventus generated expected goals of 2.25 against 1.72 for Rennes. They also had 54% of possession. Rennes took more shots, 16 to 14, and put more on target, five to four. Juventus were caught offside three times, while the visitors were never flagged. Abdelhamid Aït Boudlal was booked in the 82nd minute for time wasting.

Both sides were short of key players. Spalletti was without the injured Locatelli, Yildiz, Thuram, Grabara, Ekhator and Conceição. Zhegrova and Milik were unavailable because they are not on the UEFA squad list. Antonio Stefano Merola was in the 21-man squad after his first senior call-up. Rennes were missing their leading scorer Lepaul, who was injured and did not travel from France.

FT |⌛️| Finisce in parità all’Allianz Stadium#JuveSRFC #UEL pic.twitter.com/QaF2LuUDp9

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) October 22, 2026

Krogh had refereed nine Europa League matches and one Champions League match before this game. He had never taken charge of either club.

Juventus’s next Europa League fixtures are away to AZ Alkmaar on 5 November 2026 and at home to Omonia on 26 November 2026. Before that, Serie A resumes. Lecce host Juventus on matchday 8, with Eusebio Di Francesco’s side kicking off against Spalletti’s at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday 25 October.

#1590. Meet Brighton's merry band of unlikely heroes: a midfielder taking tips from Lionel Messi, a twinkle-toed son of a ballerina and the £3m bargain now running the Premier League

Published: 02:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 02:00 EST, 6 November 2026

Noel Gallagher arrived at the Etihad Stadium at the weekend hoping to witness a repeat of his beloved Manchester City's FA Cup triumph, only to be sent packing to the soundtrack of the High Flying Seagulls.

That has been the story – no, not morning glory – of Brighton's season. Fabian Hurzeler's side sit third and are beginning to build a compelling case as the Premier League's most unexpected title challengers since Leicester City's remarkable triumph a decade ago.

Even Danny Murphy, rarely one for lavish praise, was impressed by what he saw after the City win.

'They are such a smart team and they are an absolute pleasure to watch with the ball,' he said on BBC's Match of the Day. 'They are brave. They find a way. They are tactically very good.

'No worries who they are playing. There's no respect. They were willing to risk losing to win and that is what you want.'

Brighton's squad is packed with a number of unknowns, courtesy of a scouting network that has been unearthing gems from across the globe for years. This time, though, with an energetic, charismatic coach in Hurzeler and a perfect blend of youth and experience, there is a growing sense that all the pieces may be coming together at exactly the right moment.

Here, Daily Mail Sport's football reporter Tara Anson-Walsh takes a look at the players driving Brighton's unlikely title charge and the stories behind how they ended up on the south coast...

Brighton's squad remains packed with a number of unknowns, courtesy of a scouting network that has been unearthing gems from across the globe for years

With an energetic, charismatic coach in Hurzeler and a perfect blend of youth and experience, there is a growing sense that all the pieces may be coming together at the right moment

A central tenet of Brighton's success this season, 24-year-old Verbruggen has six clean sheets in the Premier League, the joint-most alongside Arsenal's David Raya.

The Dutchman began his career with hometown club NAC Breda before moving to Belgium in 2020. Admired by former Seagulls boss Roberto De Zerbi for his ability to play out from the back, 6ft 4in Verbruggen arrived in England in 2023 for £16.3million, a Belgian league record fee for a goalkeeper.

Three years on, the player who grew up idolising Edwin van der Sar is unsurprisingly being mooted by Real Madrid as a potential long-term replacement for Thibaut Courtois, while Bayern Munich and Tottenham also retain an interest.

Verbruggen has six clean sheets in the Premier League, the joint-most alongside David Raya

The twinkle-toed 27-year-old owes his deft feet to his mother, a professional ballerina who travelled the world performing, as well as to a childhood spent playing tennis in the Netherlands.

After a difficult initial transition from the Eredivisie to Turkey in 2018, the arrival of Vitor Pereira at Fenerbahce in 2021 and a move to wing-back proved the catalyst for Kadioglu's rapid rise.

Brighton regarded the Turkey international's versatility as a key asset. Capable of operating at either full-back position or in midfield, he joined for £25m in the summer of 2024 after impressing at the Euros as one of Hurzeler's first defensive signings.

Kadioglu owes his deft feet to his mother, a professional ballerina who travelled the world performing, as well as to a childhood spent playing tennis in the Netherlands

For a 19-year-old, Vuskovic has already seen his fair share of the world, gaining experience in Poland, Belgium and Germany after emerging as one of Croatia's brightest talents at Hajduk Split.

After becoming the youngest-ever player to feature in the Croatian top flight, the then 16-year-old was snapped up by Tottenham in 2023 and sent out immediately on loan to Hamburg when he joined the north London club two years later.

There, Vuskovic enhanced his reputation as a robust defender, aerial threat and aggressive presser. Brighton subsequently opted to break the bank, paying a club-record £50m and offering the promise of first-team football to secure his signature.

Brighton paid a club-record £50m to Tottenham for 19-year-old centre back Vuskovic's services, sealing the deal with the promise of first-team football

Brighton through and through, Dunk joined the club from Wimbledon's academy aged 12 and has gone on to make 531 appearances under nine managers before being rewarded with the captain's armband in 2019.

Born in the city to a father who played non-League football in Sussex, Dunk has been the one constant throughout Brighton's rise from League One to Europe. Unfazed both on and off the pitch, there is a running joke in the Dunk family that he doesn't reply to his text messages for five days.

Now entering the twilight of his career, Dunk remains the embodiment of the club's modern success, while Hurzeler relies on his influence to remind the younger players of its humble beginnings.

Dunk has been the one constant throughout Brighton's rise from League One to Europe since joining from Wimbledon aged 12

The France youth international grew up among the sports cars and yachts of Monte Carlo and broke through at nearby Nice before signing for PSV Eindhoven in 2019.

Admired within Brighton's headquarters for his versatility, particularly his ability to play across the back line, Boscagli was a long-term target. Despite not being the tallest defender at 5ft 11in, his impressive spring gives him a strong aerial success rate, while his comfort on the ball was another attribute the Seagulls coveted. Brighton tested PSV Eindhoven's resolve across multiple transfer windows before finally landing their man on a free transfer last year.

After a rocky first season largely spent on the bench last term under Hurzeler, Boscagli spent this summer doing the hard yards, checking in for pre-season already at, in his words, 'close to 100 per cent fitness', a trick which has certainly paid off. Moved from centre back to left-back this season, Boscagli has since appeared in every game.

Admired within Brighton's headquarters for his versatility, particularly his ability to play across the back line, Boscagli was a long-term target

It is no coincidence that Brighton's title charge has coincided with Pascal Gross's dazzling return from an 18-month stint at his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in January. Ageing 'like a fine wine', Hurzeler recently said of the 35-year-old.

Gross has quite literally run the show this season, covering the most distance of any Premier League player, running 107.4km across the opening nine games.

A little-heralded German from Ingolstadt, Gross caught the eye of the Seagulls after managing to record more chances than any other player in the Bundesliga in the 2016-17 season despite his side getting relegated, and became the Seagulls' first-ever Premier League signing at £3m.

Despite the youth of their manager, Brighton have long prized the importance of experienced players, and Gross has brought this in abundance back to the south coast.

Gross has quite literally run the show this season, covering the most distance of any Premier League player, running 107.4km across the opening nine games

The Mali-born midfielder was plucked out of obscurity by Gothenburg two years ago, bringing him in from Ivorian side ASEC Mimosas, the club where former Manchester City icon Yaya Toure began his career.

Two years and a small sample size of just 15 senior appearances later, Brighton deployed their similarly talented scouting methods to bring Yalcouye to the Premier League. An immediate loan to Sturm Graz ensued, where he ended the season as the Bundesliga Young Player of the Year after being deployed as a box-to-box midfielder, a defensive midfielder and an out-and-out winger down both flanks.

This was followed by a disappointing campaign at Swansea last term, where he started just ten Championship matches as a holding midfielder.

Injuries to key players this season have seen Yalcouye thrust into the No10 role for the first time, and it appears Hurzeler may have accidentally stumbled upon a winning formula, with the 20-year-old recording three goals in 15 appearances in all competitions and emerging as one of Brighton's standout performers so far this season.

The 20-year-old has recorded three goals in 15 appearances in all competitions and emerging as one of Brighton's standout performers so far this season

The Paraguay midfielder joined as a 21-year-old from Lionel Messi's Inter Miami last January and hasn't looked back, notching ten goals and one assist in his first full season at the club.

'He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,' Gomez said of the Argentine in an interview soon after joining, a sentiment which clearly resonated as he proceeded to shoot, and score, from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month.

Gomez, who broke through the ranks at Libertad in 2022, was admired for his impressive stamina as well as his physicality, an asset which Brighton felt would help him transition well into the Premier League.

Able to cover large areas of the pitch while remaining aggressive in pressing and duels, Brighton have been left clearly satisfied with the reported MLS record £11m they paid for him, and which will undoubtedly skyrocket amid reports he is drawing admirers from AC Milan and Atletico Madrid.

The Paraguay midfielder joined as a 21-year-old from Lionel Messi's Inter Miami last January and hasn't looked back, notching ten goals and one assist in his first full season at the club

Born into a footballing family, Ayari's Tunisian father travelled to Sweden to become a footballer in his youth, and although this wasn't a success, his dream transferred to his two sons, with Ayari's younger brother plying his trade at AIK, in the Swedish top flight.

It was while a 21-year-old Yasin was also at AIK that he was spotted by Brighton's technical team, who admired his versatility and technical skill, traits which have been honed by Brighton's attack-minded, possession-based style of play.

The £3.5m signing spent a difficult first full season on loan in the Championship split across Coventry and Blackburn, although Ayari now credits that period for developing his mental resilience as he was handed a fresh start following the arrival of Hurzeler.

The £3.5m signing spent a difficult first full season on loan in the Championship at Coventry and Blackburn, although Ayari now credits that period for developing his mental resilience

Defensive frailties last season at left back, the position he had been signed to play in, meant that Maxim De Cuyper slipped down the pecking order at the Amex and saw his game time limited.

Yet injuries to wingers Yankuba Minteh and Kaoru Mitoma have seen the 25-year-old grasp an opportunity to play higher up the pitch with both hands, recording four goals and four assists in 14 appearances.

Developed through his childhood side Club Brugge's academy, De Cuyper played as a winger until he was 14, and his form in that position this season will certainly be giving Hurzeler something to think about when his two explosive wingers return from injury.

Yet injuries to wingers Yankuba Minteh and Kaoru Mitoma have seen the 25-year-old grasp an opportunity to play higher up the pitch with both hands

The then 18-year-old was signed last summer for £31.4m, Brighton's fourth-most expensive signing and a hefty investment in a teenager who had spent just one season in senior football.

But the Seagulls were investing in potential, and Kostoulas had just enjoyed an impressive breakthrough season at the club he had been at since he was 12, Olympiakos, scoring seven league goals - including one in the play-offs - as the Athens side won the Greek Super League.

Recognised for his ability to play in all positions across the front line, Kostoulas was admired by Brighton for his technical skill in linking play, beating defenders, as well as boasting the physicality of a player beyond his years.

He has already surpassed last season's tally of two goals with three, plus a further three assists, in his opening nine appearances in the Premier League, and Brighton fans will be anticipating much more to come from this exciting youngster.

#1589. Sky Germany: Krösche-Hardung double hire now a ‘concrete option’ for Milan – the situation

A leading source in Germany has confirmed that Timmo Hardung could be joining Markus Krösche as a new member of AC Milan’s management.

It has not been a secret that Milan wanted to hire Krösche, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Earlier in the week, the reliable Matteo Moretto announced that Milan have an agreement in place with Krösche to become the new Head of Football. Not only that, but he claimed that the compensation had been agreed with Eintracht Frankfurt too.

One of the other interesting discussion points has been whether Hardung might come with him, a sporting director who has been labelled Krösche’s right-hand man given their work together at RB Leipzig and in Frankfurt.

Now, Florian Plettenberg of Sky Germany has also confirmed the reports doing the rounds which suggest Hardung could follow his close friend to Italy.

“Should Timmo Hardung not remain at Eintracht Frankfurt as sporting director, a move to AC Milan alongside Markus Krösche is a concrete option, as reported. Milan’s current priority is to reach a full agreement with Krösche/Eintracht as soon as possible,” he said.

#1588. Celik and Nico Gonzalez injuries add to Juventus absences before Lecce

Juventus will travel to Lecce without Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez after both players picked up muscle injuries in Thursday’s 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes, adding two more names to an already long absence list for Luciano Spalletti.

The club confirmed the diagnoses in an official medical update on Friday, October 23. Both players had felt muscle discomfort after the Rennes match and went for tests at J|medical that morning.

According to the club, Celik has a low-grade injury to the biceps femoris in his left leg, while Nico Gonzalez has a low-grade injury to the soleus muscle in his right calf. Juventus said both players have already started their rehabilitation programmes, but the statement did not give a return date for either of them.

Medical Update | Çelik and Nico González’s conditions

🗞️ https://t.co/BHwNzeidQ7 pic.twitter.com/YUXRK97IwL

— JuventusFC 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@juventusfcen) October 23, 2026

The timing is frustrating for Celik in particular. The Turkish full-back opened the scoring against Rennes in the fifth minute, converting a pass from Nick Woltemade, before being taken off at half-time. You can read how the rest of that night unfolded in our report on the Rennes draw.

Juventus have not put a timeframe on either recovery, so any estimate comes from the Italian press. Virgilio Sport reports that both players are expected to be out for around 20 days and should only return after the November international break, with the home game against Venezia on November 22 named as the first realistic target.

If that estimate holds, the pair would miss the trip to Lecce, the meeting with Genoa, the home game against Napoli, the Europa League visit to AZ Alkmaar and the match with Fiorentina. That is a demanding run to face with a thinner squad, and it comes at a point when Juventus are trying to recover from the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio.

Celik and Nico Gonzalez join Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Francisco Conceicao on the sidelines, according to Tuttosport. Conceicao is already in rehabilitation after the shoulder problem he picked up against Lazio, as covered in our Francisco Conceicao injury update.

Tuttosport’s expected line-up has Spalletti sticking with a 3-5-2, with Pierre Kalulu and Andrea Cambiaso on the flanks and Woltemade partnering Randal Kolo Muani in attack. The match at the Via del Mare kicks off at 18:00 Italian time on Sunday, October 25, with Maresca as referee.

Supporters will also have to wait until matchday to hear from the coach. Tuttosport reports that Spalletti, in agreement with the club, will not hold his usual press conference on the eve of the Lecce game. The paper links the decision to the packed schedule after the Europa League fixture, and Virgilio Sport notes that Spalletti has taken the same approach before during congested spells, with no controversy behind the choice.

The squeeze on the squad is now the bigger story. With two more first-team players ruled out and the injury list still growing, Spalletti will need his remaining options to carry the load through a busy stretch of Serie A and European fixtures before the international break.

Sources: Juventus FC, Tuttosport, Virgilio Sport

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1587. Champions League draw: Arsenal to renew Mourinho rivalry with Real Madrid tie

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage. Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

Verdict Playing against the European champions and travelling to Barcelona will be a true test of how much progress Enzo Maresca has made in the short time he has been at the Etihad Stadium. City’s other games do not look easy either but they should be defeating teams such as Sporting Lisbon and Porto – at least they would be expected to under Pep Guardiola.

Verdict The San Siro was where Arne Slot began to turn results around last season and Iraola getting a win there would be a big statement. Atlético staged a comeback at Anfield in 2020 and the repeat fixture will be tight. But there are enough winnable games there for Liverpool to reach the next round.

Verdict They will face a wall of noise in Istanbul when they play Galatasaray, but Villa will look to get points from the game. There are some tasty destinations for travelling fans and getting results there will ease the pressure on the match against PSG, who have been rattled by Villa before but remain a difficult opponent. The Nou Camp is a place where momentum can change in a season – for good or bad.

Verdict The repeat of the 1999 final is the standout fixture, but Michael Carrick should be looking beyond that match for the points needed to progress. He has been given a tough set of away games to navigate. They are winnable but difficult. So those games at Old Trafford will be very important.

That brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January.

The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

So we have 144 fixtures decided but there are certainly a few heavyweight contests which stand out:

That brings the draw to an end! Just a reminder that the order of the fixtures is based on the pots and the respective home and away fixtures within the pots, rather than chronology.

That is pots two and three done. Just the pot four teams to sort out now, finding out which other pot four teams they will face.

Some crackers in there. Up next we will be finding out all the opponents for the pot two teams.

There is a fairly extensive video explanation of the format currently taking place. We should you be bringing you some fixtures very shortly...

The draw is now getting underway. Uefa deputy general secretary Giorgio Marchetti comes on stage to oversee proceedings. A reminder of the format:

The 36 teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

CONFIRMED: #UCLdraw pots for the league phase 👀 pic.twitter.com/LpMjiap6RF

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

But before the draw we will be hearing from Villa about the 2011 final, which he scored in as Barcelona dismantled Manchester United at Wembley.

He calls it a “great generation” of players, mentioning Lionel Messi, who also scored in the 3-1 win.

Henry will be part of the draw so he remains on stage as Ceferin departs. David Villa will also be coming onto the stage to help with proceedings. We are told the draw will be starting shortly.

We’re hearing from Henry now about losing the 2006 Champions League final with Arsenal and winning three years later with Barcelona.

He’s now discussing the current Arsenal crop and how they are getting closer to the trophy. He says if “they keep their core” and make some additions they can get over the line. But PSG “are an annoying team at the moment”.

Marquinhos on winning the respect award: “I’m very happy and honoured to be given this trophy. Fair play is an essential part of both football and daily life, and I will keep being respectful this year.”

Up next is the “Uefa President’s Award”? The winner is of course Thierry Henry and, fortunately, he is in attendance, so he’s up on the stage to collect this honour. A slow clap from Martin Keown in the crowd.

Reshmin Chowdhury and Pedro Pinto shuffle the musicians off the stage before outlining this evening’s itinerary.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is then brought up to the stage, after a quiet summer, to announce Marquinhos as the winner of a new award, the Respect Beyond the Game award.

Marquinhos is not at the ceremony, so it will be PSG president Nasser Al-Khelaifi coming up to collect it. We hear from the defender on a video message.

The ceremony is underway in Monaco with a live performance of the famous anthem – orchestra and all – while pictures of previous winners play on the big screen in the background.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. There are five English teams involved in the Champions League this season – one short of the Premier League’s tally from last term.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Liverpool will be in pot one, while Manchester United and Aston Villa will be in pot two.

This evening’s ceremony should be getting underway in Monaco in a couple of minutes.

All set for this evening's #UCL draw in Monaco 📌🏆 pic.twitter.com/N3verDUO9y

Paris St-Germain will be aiming to become the first team to win three successive Champions Leagues since Real Madrid’s run of titles between 2016 and 2018.

The holders 🔴🔵#UCLdraw pic.twitter.com/eB05BNfWZi

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

Similarly, Arsenal will not be travelling to San Siro to face Inter, but could host the Serie A champions at the Emirates.

Arsenal finished top of the league phase last season after winning all eight fixtures and it resulted in a favourable run to the final, facing Bayer Leverkusen, Sporting and Atletico Madrid.

Liverpool, meanwhile, topped the league phase in the 2024-25 campaign – the first season with the new format – but fell at the first hurdle in the knockout stages after being drawn against Paris St-Germain.

The Ligue 1 side have proven that it’s not essential to be firing the whole way through the tournament, finishing 15th and 11th in the league phase in the last two seasons but going on to lift the trophy on both occasions.

Mattéo Guendouzi, the former Arsenal fireband, was at the heart of chaotic and ugly scenes in the Champions League qualifying play-off between Lyon and his side Fenerbahce, culminating in a brawl at the mouth of the tunnel.

Guendouzi provoked Lyon fans as he slowly made his way off the pitch in the aftermath of a 2-1 victory at the Groupama Stadium that sent the Turkish outfit through to the Champions League group stage.

Matteo Guendouzi has not forgotten who his rivals are... 👀The former Marseille player made his feelings known as Fenerbahce knocked out Marseille's rivals Lyon. pic.twitter.com/pjDKPqPzZD

As he gestured towards the fans, while being shepherded by team-mates, objects were thrown from the crowd. A figure in what appears to be a Lyon tracksuit then emerged from the tunnel and seemed to try to aim a flying kick at Guendouzi.

Of the 36 teams in the draw, 29 qualified at the end of last season, while the remaining seven places were decided by play-offs.

AEK, LASK, Viking, Slovan Bratislava, Sabah Baku, Fenerbahce and Bodo/Glimt were the seven teams to come through the play-offs.

Hello and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the Champions League draw in Monaco, with the 36 teams in this season’s competition finding out their eight league phase fixtures.

The teams will be split into four pots of nine, based on “club coefficient rankings”, with defending champions Paris St-Germain automatically named as the top seed.

Liverpool, Manchester City and Arsenal will be among the teams joining the Parisians in pot one, while the two remaining English teams, Manchester United and Aston Villa, will be in pot two.

Proceedings will begin with a team from pot one being drawn at random, and they will be allocated eight fixtures – four at home and four away – by an automated software. They will face two teams from each pot, with one home game and one away game per pot, while they cannot play a team from their country.

This will be done for all nine teams from pot one, before the same process takes place for pot two teams, though they will already know their pot one opponents. Pot three teams will then find out their pot three and four opponents, before the pot four sides are allocated their fixtures against each other.

This season is the third under the new format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

For example, Liverpool cannot host Real Madrid in the league phase this term after welcoming the 15-time European champions to Anfield at this stage of the previous two campaigns. Andoni Iraola’s side could, however, travel to the Bernabeu for an away meeting with Madrid.

The league phase will kick off on 8 September and will be wrapped up after all teams play at the same time on 27 January. The top eight teams of the league phase progress to the last 16 automatically, while teams that finish between ninth and 24th will be forced to navigate a play-off tie to reach the knockout stages.

The draw is expected to get underway at 5pm.

#1586. Lecce vs Juventus: in-form hosts await Spalletti’s stretched side at the Via del Mare

Juventus face Lecce at the Stadio Via del Mare this evening, and the fixture arrives at an awkward moment for Luciano Spalletti. His side are still looking for a first win since the 3-0 home defeat by Lazio, while Di Francesco’s Lecce come into Matchday 8 on the back of their most convincing result of the season.

Kick-off is at 18:00 Italian time, which is 17:00 in the UK and Ireland.

Lecce travelled to Udinese last weekend and came away with a 3-0 victory. According to Flashscore, Kialonda Gaspar headed in the opener from a Gallo corner in the 14th minute, and N’Dri doubled the lead in the 25th minute after Tiago Gabriel had gone up for a header. Siebert added the third four minutes from time after a ball was won from Ekkelenkamp.

It was Lecce’s first win in Udine for six years and handed Udinese a fifth straight league defeat. Fatah also hit the crossbar, so the margin could have been even wider. For a side that has spent much of its recent history fighting at the wrong end of the table, it was a timely lift before the visit of Juventus.

The picture is very different in Turin. The heavy home loss to Lazio was followed by a 2-2 draw with Rennes in the Europa League, and the injury list has kept growing. Zeki Celik and Nico Gonzalez are the latest names to drop out, as covered in our Celik and Nico Gonzalez injury update, and Spalletti chose not to give a pre-match press conference on Saturday.

The Lazio defeat in Turin left Juventus well short of the Serie A leaders, so Sunday is about more than one result. Three points in Puglia would ease some of the pressure that has built up over the past week.

Juventus do not have to look far back for a good memory of this trip. The club’s own retrospective recalls the Matchday 36 meeting at the Via del Mare in May 2026, when Dusan Vlahovic scored after just 12 seconds. Kenan Yildiz started the move, Teun Koopmeiners was involved in the build-up and Andrea Cambiaso delivered the ball for Vlahovic to finish into the roof of the net.

That game stayed lively. Michele Di Gregorio had to make a fine save at the other end, Francisco Conceicao struck the crossbar and Vlahovic had another good chance, all inside the first six minutes. Pierre Kalulu thought he had added a second with around half an hour to play, but VAR ruled it out for a marginal Vlahovic offside in the build-up. The early goal proved enough for the win.

Several of the players involved that day, including Yildiz and Conceicao, are now injured, which shows how much Spalletti’s options have changed since May.

Tuttosport reports that Maresca will referee the match. In Italy it is live on DAZN and Sky. In the United Kingdom the game is shown on DAZN UK and Prime Video UK, in Ireland on DAZN, and in the United States on Paramount+, fuboTV and Peacock, according to the club’s broadcast guide.

Sources: Juventus FC, Juventus FC broadcast guide, Flashscore

At Juve FC, Luca covers match analysis, squad news, and the longer threads that run through a Juventus season. He writes with the perspective of someone who genuinely cares about where the club is heading rather than simply reporting what has already happened. His focus tends to lean toward how the team sets up, where things break down, and what needs to change to get back to where Juventus belongs in the European conversation.

#1585. Sydney FC fans vow to return to the stands after ugly clash with police sparked calls for boycott

Published: 01:23 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 03:07 EST, 6 November 2026

Sydney FC's active supporter group The Cove will return to the stands for the first time since October's derby, following a bitter dispute over allegations police assaulted a teenage fan and handcuffed supporter leaders before throwing them out.

The group will be back for Friday night’s match against Central Coast Mariners at Allianz Stadium in Moore Park, Sydney, after talks involving the club, NSW Police, Venues NSW and stadium security.

The Cove had threatened to boycott matches after the October 16 derby with Western Sydney Wanderers, accusing police of the 'worst policing standards' in the fixture’s 14-year history and demanding the club defend its fans.

Its return comes amid a broader push for reform, with Football Supporters Association Australia declaring that repeated reviews and weekly discussions with police are no longer sufficient.

The dispute followed a scoreless derby attended by more than 30,000 spectators at Allianz Stadium.

The Cove alleged a 17-year-old supporter was repeatedly slammed into safe-standing rails by police before being struck in the back of the head.

Sydney FC supporter group The Cove will return to Allianz Stadium following a bitter dispute over policing at October's derby

It also claimed two chant leaders, known as capos, were removed from the stadium, while five members of its leadership were handcuffed, pressed against walls and ejected without subsequently being charged.

According to the group's statement, officers later told those leadership members: 'We have nothing to legally charge you with, move on.'

The Cove alleged other supporters were also ejected without justification and accused police of antagonising fans rather than protecting them.

Daily Mail has contacted NSW Police for comment.

The Cove supporters' anger extended to Sydney FC, the APL and stadium officials, whom it challenged to intervene.

'Whilst you may stay silent and not fight for your fans, don't come crying if we don't show up,' the group said.

'Active support isn't a crime. Back your f*****g fans.'

At the centre of the dispute was The Cove's allegation that police ignored established arrangements for supporter marshals to help resolve issues in the stands.

The Cove accused police of bypassing supporter marshals during the October 16 clash with Western Sydney Wanderers

The group claimed marshalls and stadium security were overridden, with officers instead entering supporter bays and taking action without consultation.

'Nobody should be made to feel like a criminal for wanting to passionately support their club,' it said.

Sydney FC initially responded by saying it was investigating the allegations with Venues NSW, the APL and NSW Police.

A joint statement released by the club and The Cove on November 5 said subsequent discussions had produced a commitment to stronger communication, mutual respect and clearer matchday processes.

'All parties have agreed on the importance of active support to football in this country, and all believe passionate, active support and a safe matchday experience must go hand in hand,' it said.

The club thanked The Cove's leadership for its professional engagement, while the supporter group thanked Sydney FC for listening to members and standing alongside them.

The statement welcomed fans back but did not announce findings on the alleged derby incidents or specify changes to police operations.

In a subsequent Instagram post, The Cove said it wanted to ensure there was never a repeat of the round-one incidents.

The supporters will return for Sydney FC's clash with Central Coast Mariners at Allianz Stadium in Moore Park

'We are hopeful that future policing at games will reflect the efforts made by the club, and Cove leadership,' it said.

'We will be monitoring the progress closely over the coming rounds.'

The dispute has also drawn intervention from the FSAA, which says supporters elsewhere in Australia and New Zealand share concerns about excessive police and security actions.

In an open letter published on November 5, the association welcomed Western Sydney Wanderers chairman Paul Lederer's criticism of police treatment of his club's fans.

It said APL leaders shared its frustration, but argued the response needed to go beyond discussions after each incident.

'We are now at the point where reactive reviews and weekly chats with police following regular operational failures on match day are simply insufficient,' the association wrote.

The FSAA said it had recommended structural changes in 2025, including rapid response protocols, measures to prevent supporters being demonised and better communication between authorities and fan groups.

It is now pushing for a framework involving senior league management, clubs, supporter leaders, stadium operators, private security and state police commands.

#1584. Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells on rough textured substrates are at present limited by a critical trade-off in self-assembled monolayer (SAM) design because increasing molecular conjugation enhances conductivity but often leads to unfavourable aggregation that impairs conformal coverage1,2. Here we overcome this challenge using a rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation that incorporates tailored intramolecular distortion to suppress excess π–π stacking without sacrificing charge-transport efficiency. This steric regulation facilitates the formation of a highly ordered, conformal SAM across rough pyramidal textures. By reconciling molecular packing with interfacial coverage, the tailored interface provides optimized energy-level alignment for ultrafast charge extraction, enables improved defect passivation through adaptive conformational adjustment and acts as a robust template for high-quality perovskite film growth. Making use of this interface, the optimized tandem device achieves a notable fill factor (FF) of 85%, yielding a certified stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 35.1%. Furthermore, the device demonstrates outstanding stability, retaining more than 94% of its initial performance after 1,500 h of ageing under the ISOS-L-1 protocol. Our findings provide a clear molecular engineering route to reconcile conductivity and film uniformity while maximizing the performance of tandem photovoltaics on textured silicon substrates.

#1583. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Five things we learned – battery life, the marksman and the core five

AC Milan managed to get the win that they needed going into the international break, but they certainly made hard work of it.

Things were going very well at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris against an in-form Genoa side, with Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic giving Milan a two-goal lead with less than 20 minutes on the clock. Both goals came from the high press, with Ruben Amorim’s side looking full of energy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, as has been the theme this year, the Rossoneri were unable to turn it into a complete performance. The second-half drop-off saw Genoa build more and more pressure, with Ellertsson’s strike from range making it a nervy finish.

Milan held on to secure a win that gets them back into the top four for now, and the search for consistency can resume after the two-week break. Oli Fisher has five things were learned from the game at the Marassi.

We are running out of words to describe this debut season for Alphadjo Cisse. If it wasn’t certain from the sample size we had already, then the Bologna games and this one today were proof that he is a right-place, right-time player.

The young Italian was perfectly positioned for Rabiot’s pull-back in the opening exchanges, as he so often is. He ghosts into scoring areas and provides the killer touch, with the goal this afternoon being perhaps his most impressive so far: a first-time finish across his body right into the corner.

The cynical side of us wants to say that Goncalo Ramos could learn a thing or two about what spots to be in inside the box, though the defence of the Portuguese is that his movement often creates these pockets of space to attack.

Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8). He also matched Andriy Shevchenko’s eight goals in his first 13 games for the Diavolo.

Another remarkable stat is that the 20-year-old has scored his eight goals across all competitions from just 20 shots. Some might argue that kind of hit rate is unsustainable, but it shows no signs of stopping for now.

As mentioned in the introduction, the first-half performance from Amorim’s side was something that fans can really get behind. It was intense, aggressive and front-footed. The quality wasn’t always there to turn everything into danger, but the intent was there.

In fact, it was this tenacity that yielded the two goals. The first one came after Pulisic pressed and won back possession, allowing Rabiot to square for Cisse. Then, the press again forced an error from Genoa with Ostigard’s stray pass seized by Ramos, who squared for Pulisic to net.

It serves as categorical proof that something energy levels alone can be enough to get Milan into very good positions in games. Yet, we also saw the other side of things too: when the battery runs flat, the Rossoneri can lose control of games very quickly.

As a result of this, where more polished teams might see things out comfortably or even score more goals, Milan seem to sink into a hole of self-doubt, inviting pressure through a quite obvious inability to cycle the ball and keep opponents at bay.

Injuries are partly to blame for this, because not having versatile options like Fikayo Tomori, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Alexis Saelemaekers to bring on is hurting things. The bench on paper looked very weak, and those who did come in didn’t really help the chaos.

This is what Amorim refers to when he talks about the team not being ‘ready’. For various reasons – from the treatment room being full to the team not being fully cohesive – Milan’s level fluctuates wildly both within games and from match to match.

There was a report in La Gazzetta dello Sport this morning which highlighted a rather remarkable statistic. With Luka Modric, Mario Gila and Pulisic all not in the starting line-up, Milan are yet to pick up a single point.

This is arguably the crux of the rotation issue; the idea that managing the conditions of certain players is a necessity but upsetting the spine of the team is running a big risk. We’d like to add Rabiot and Diego Moreira into the mix too, as the five players Milan cannot do without.

The Spanish centre-back, the Croatian and French midfield duo, the Belgian wing-back and the American forward are simply too important. Their presence is vital not just because of their quality and propensity to provide decisive contributions, but because they are among the select group who can actually play Amorim’s way.

Each of them had a positive performance for various reasons. Gila’s fierce competitive nature facilitates the high line, Modric is the only one skilled in ball management, Rabiot is so wise when it comes to taking up the right positions, while Moreira and Pulisic are the technical sparks.

These are the players to build around from now until the end of season, while then waiting to see what the windows bring. When any combination of those five are playing, Milan’s limitations are often brutally exposed.

MilanNews described the performance from referee Davide Massa as a ‘disaster’, and we think that is being quite generous. The experienced official never once gave the impression of having control over a game where the pace and ferocity demanded it.

There is of course the one incident that everyone is talking about: the yellow card for Marcandalli after he brought Rabiot down. From our perspective, there are absolutely no doubts about it being a sending off.

The rules for DOGSO (Denial of a Goal Scoring Opportunity) take into account distance from goal, but the Frenchman and Cisse were about to have a two-on-zero attack with the entire half to run into. There is no way Ostigard was getting back to cover, and we question why VAR did not intervene.

To make matters worse, he then dished out a yellow card to Rabiot for rightfully protesting, and gave red cards to three of the Milan coaching staff too. In general Massa’s refereeing left a lot to be desired as there was no consistency in the fouls that he was whistling, and the five yellow cards the Rossoneri got felt disproportionate to Genoa’s two.

Thankfully the Diavolo were able to get over the line and bank the win, but if things had taken a more negative turn in the second half, we would be talking about that Marcandalli incident with a lot more venom.

Koni De Winter showed up in a big way against his old club, putting in another top performance in a week where he has been linked with a move to three big Premier League clubs.

Yet, we have to question the highs and lows. To best illustrate this, here are our ratings for the Belgian from each of the last four games.

vs. Bologna: Where to begin? I think he could have done better positioning-wise on Bologna’s first, with no one else to mark in the box, and then he completely gifted the free-kick that made it 2-1 for the guests. Some good moments too, but too many mistakes tonight. Maybe a 4.5?

vs. Inter (8): He absolutely won the battle against Thuram this game and it’s not like it was an easy one either. The two had several 50-50 duels and he always came out on top. Aside from his Thuram battle, he was very good overall and deserves a high rating here.

vs. Ferencvaros (5.5): That backpass for Torriani should never be played in that way, even if Maignan is between the sticks. He admittedly got a bit unlucky with his clearance in the second half, but even then perhaps he could have done better. Anyway, for me it’s the pass which brings his rating down.

vs. Genoa (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Being the central centre-back is a position that carries a lot of weight and responsibility in Amorim’s system, and what is clear is that one game De Winter can look like the perfect man for the job, and in others he looks simply unplayable (and not in the good way).

One of the reasons for these wild fluctuations could also be because the former Juventus man simply hasn’t had a break. So, it is easy to see why the management are targeting a central defender ahead of January, someone who can give everyone a breather and help keep the levels high.

#1582. Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

He said: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

Sage said: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

“I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”

“It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a new manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”

“We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”

"I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ

"Say what you actually mean!" 🤣Erling Haaland takes over Rayan Cherki's post-match interview! pic.twitter.com/adW6IU8DzQ

2 + 2 - Rayan Cherki is the third player to have a game with multiple goals and another game with multiple assists across a team's first two matches of a Premier League campaign, after Thierry Henry in 2004-05 and Didier Drogba in 2010-11.Polymath. pic.twitter.com/4cRV0xMIFa

September 5: Fulham vs Crystal PalaceSeptember 12: Crystal Palace vs IpswichSeptember 19: Leeds vs Crystal PalaceOctober 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham ForestOctober 18: Brighton vs Crystal Palace

Pierre Sage’s side will host Middlesbrough in the League Cup third round next month and will also begin their Europa League campaign in September.

The directions of these teams will be diverging this season. City were wonderful, free-flowing, expressive and fun to watch. Palace not so much. It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

"Cherki was the difference" 🪄"He is a genius" 🧠Jamie Redknapp reacts to Crystal Palace 1-4 Man City 🔊 pic.twitter.com/UjSarMngDR

September 5: Manchester City vs CoventrySeptember 13: Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20: Manchester City vs SunderlandOctober 11: Liverpool vs Manchester CityOctober 17: Manchester City vs Ipswich

Manchester City will take on Norwich in the League Cup third round in September and will also have their first Champions League match next month.

Saturday:Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestBournemouth vs EvertonCoventry vs Hull CityTottenham vs Newcastle

Possession: Crystal Palace 28%-72% Manchester CityShots: 9-18Shots on target: 1-9Corners: 2-6Touches in the opposition box: 13-33

Pretty comprehensive in Manchester City’s favour, which is reflected in the scoreline.

The final whistle is blown at Selhurst Park and Manchester City have cruised to a 4-1 win thanks to doubles from Cherki and Haaland. Enzo Maresca’s side make it two wins from two whereas it is two defeats from two for Pierre Sage.

Manchester City, with the three points already in the bag, are just stroking the ball around with ease and are in complete control. Palace can barely get a foot on it.

A late double substitution for Manchester City as Reis and Braithwaite come on. Enzo Maresca’s side are cruising to victory to make it two wins from two.

Cherki has two goals to his name and now Haaland does as Manchester City are romping to victory in south London. Guehi wins possession for City inside the Palace half and the ball comes to Foden, who dribbles towards the Palace penalty area. He lays it off to his left to Haaland who, from a narrow angle, finds the root of the net.

Erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF

Nearly an instant impact from McAidoo as the 18-year-old drives through the Palace half and curls a shot from the edge of the box that goes just wide.

When Manchester City were making those substitutions, the Crystal Palace fans were making sure they let the officials know how long the Manchester City players were taking to get off.

There is going to be a debut for the Premier League’s most expensive teenager ever as Bouaddi comes on for Manchester City. McAidoo is also coming on, with Cherki and Anderson going off.

Mingueza eventually comes on but not after having to wait until the ball goes out of play again as Khalaili was adjudged to have taken too long to have got off the pitch. Safe to say the Palace fans are not too impressed with that new rule. It will probably be a pub question in the years ahead. That change does mean that Palace have used all five substitutions, which means Munoz will not come on. He is being linked with a reunion with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest in the final days of this window.

Crystal Palace make another double change and it will be two debuts as Disasi and Mingueza come on.

Enzo Maresca turns to his bench for the first time tonight as Kovacic comes on.

Khalaili brings down Semenyo and is booked for that challenge.

Palace are going to make a double substitution as McNeil and Gozo replace Nketiah and Pino. 19-year-old Gozo is on for his Palace debut.

That was a chance for Palace. Guessand finds Pino, who drives into the Manchester City penalty area on the right. Pino has Nketiah at the far post but there is too much on the cross.

Guessand, back at Palace, is going to come on to replace Strand Larsen, who has been pretty quiet up top for the home side tonight.

Sometimes you feel blessed to witness an extraordinary moment of footballing genius. Selhurst Park has just seen two in the space of three minutes. Yeremy Pino’s free-kick which flicked off the back of Gianluigi Donnarumma was stunning, but even that could not truly compare to the slalom run of Rayan Cherki that drew a collective intake of breath from all those present. The Frenchman has just followed it with a scorching shot. It couldn’t compare with his first, though.

Three goals come in quick succession and Cherki restores Manchester City’s two-goal advantage with his second of the night. The Frenchman receives it on the turn from around 30 yards out and drives towards the Palace penalty area. He then shoots and a kind deflection off Richards takes it over Henderson’s diving effort and into the Palace net.

Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r

Just as the hosts appeared to maybe out of this one, they get a goal back. Pino’s fantastic free-kick strikes the bar, hits Donnarumma on the back before going into the net off the post. That hit the frame of the goal twice and Palace have a crucial goal, minutes after going 2-0 down.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp

Anderson brings down Pino not far outside the Manchester City penalty area and is booked.

The next goal in this game felt crucial and the visitors have it. Foden drives towards the Palace penalty area before playing a pass forward into the path of Cherki. The Frenchman has numerous defenders around but he shows neat footwork to skip past a few, holds off Richards before slotting home with his left foot.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv

No-one has had fewer touches on the pitch tonight than Haaland up until this point but the Norwegian’s goal is the difference. His number of touches (14) is the joint fewest with his compatriot Strand Larsen.

That was a good chance for Nketiah. He plays the ball to the underlapping Mitchell, who from the byline cuts it back into the path of Nketiah. The former Arsenal man should so so much better with his opportunity from the edge of the six-yard box but fires a long way wide.

Semenyo wins Manchester City an early corner in this second half off Canvot. Anderson’s delivery beyond the back post picks out O’Reilly, who in space heads back across goal but Pino heads away.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park, with Manchester City carrying a 1-0 lead into this second half. As the players emerged from the tunnels for the second half, the DJ at Selhurst Park paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers by playing Islands in the Stream. Nice touch! Get your favourite Dolly and Kenny tunes in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Crystal Palace 33%-67% Manchester CityShots: 7-11Shots on target: 1-6Corners: 2-2Touches in the opposition box: 10-18

The stats are certainly in Manchester City’s favour and they will feel they probably should have more than the one goal.

Cherki has a late chance for Manchester City but his shot is well saved by Henderson down to his right.

The first half at Selhurst Park is then brought to an end and Manchester City lead 1-0 at the break thanks to Haaland’s header.

There will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Palace started off with a nominal back three. That has become a back five far too often for Pierre Sage’s liking at times in this first half, yet still City are playing through them almost at will. The Palace fans whose deafening support accompanied Palace shots in the opening minutes are reduced to cheering battling midfield runs that win a free-kick now.

Pino delivers a free-kick into the Manchester City box and Richards gets to it first. It comes off his shoulder and rolls into the arms of Donnarumma.

Semenyo’s shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Richards, forcing Henderson into a decent save.

Palace now miss a big opportunity and should be on level terms. Wharton, who has probably been the best player on the pitch tonight, whips in a cross from the right and picks out Mitchell, who has a free header from eight yards out but somehow misses the target.

Strand Larsen comes close with a header from a Pino cross but he would have been offside anyway.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the visitors. Wharton drives forward into the Manchester City half and is cynically brought down by Cherki, who looked perplexed when the yellow card was shown but it was an obvious booking.

Foden wastes his second big chance of this first half. Manchester City break through O’Reilly, who carries it down the right. He waits for Cherki to make the overlapping run before passing to the Frenchman. Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Well, that was easy. So easy in fact – perfect Semenyo cross, perfect Haaland header - that it hushed Selhurst Park as the ball looped over Dean Henderson. Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

King Harald V of Norway has died in the last few days and over the last few hours two Norwegian cyclists claimed a one-two at the Vuelta a Espana and now Haaland has a goal.

He has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark. Semenyo is afforded too much space on the left just outside the penalty area and clips in a cross towards the far post. Haaland gets up highest, above Richards, and guides a superb header over Henderson into the Palace net.

Erling Haaland gets off the mark for the new Premier League season! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/5ZjQUVk6Zl

The England boss is in attendance tonight, perhaps keeping a close eye on that midfield battle between Anderson and Wharton.

Palace flirt with danger inside their own penalty area. After Haaland’s flick, Kamada should just belt the ball away but instead inexplicably leaves it. Henderson manages to mop up just as Foden was eyeing up the chance.

There is a mad scramble inside the Palace box but somehow the hosts escape without conceding. Initially, Anderson’s shot from range is saved by Henderson but Manchester City keep it alive in the penalty area. Palace frantically attempt to clear their lines and eventually they do after Haaland came close.

Quite a lot of the focus tonight will be on two English midfielders; one who has got a big-money move this summer and the other thus far has not. Anderson is directly up against Wharton and so far it is the latter who is winning the early battles, including dispossessing Anderson in midfield.

The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

Both sides emerge from the tunnel in the corner of Selhurst Park to the customary sound of Glad All Over and we are moments away from kick-off in south London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Crystal Palace: Henderson, Khalaili, Canvot, Richards, Tomiyasu, Mitchell, Wharton, Kamada, Pino, Strand Larsen, Nketiah.Substitutes: Benitez, Munoz, Disasi, Mingueza, Hughes, Lerma, Gozo, McNeil, Guessand.

Manchester City: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly, Anderson, Guehi, Cherki, Foden Semenyo, Haaland.Substitutes: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis.

Yes! It may have been fleeting but the boy in the Palace tracksuit top had his moment after all with Erling Haaland as City waited in line to enter the Selhurst Park pitch. And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

Crystal Palace looked set to sign Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez but that deal could be in doubt as there may be some problems with his medical. We await to see further updates on that situation.

“He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

“That is what makes me smile. I do not like watching players pass it sideways, that is not why I go to football. I go to watch geniuses do their work. Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”

"He's irreplaceable" 💥Jamie Redknapp and Clinton Morrison sing the praises of Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton 🤝 pic.twitter.com/ZOpcZcItHY

Jack Grealish is not in the Manchester City squad tonight amid links with the likes of Everton and Sunderland. Will he still be at the club beyond the deadline? It would appear not.

Both Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta are out of the Crystal Palace squad tonight with injury but could they be on the move before the window slams shut? Sarr has been linked with Galatasaray and Liverpool whilst the situation is complicated with Mateta as he claims the final year of his contract is void. How do those two situations resolve themselves? Daniel Munoz has been linked with a move to Nottingham Forest but is on the bench for Palace this evening.

An unfulfilled wish so far for a young Palace fan holding up a child’s red Norway shirt with ‘Haaland’ emblazoned on it. Having waited patiently for the City players to emerge for their warm-up and being held by his dad as he leant over the stone wall to attract Haaland’s attention, he was left disappointed because the City striker was simply not looking as he and his teammates jogged past. Will the boy, who has on a Palace tracksuit top, get a photo with his hero when the striker returns to the Portakabin that hosts the away dressing room prior to kick-off? Stay tuned.

Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

“We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old showed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.
